articles.title: Cambodia's floating schools hit by rising fuel costs
articles.summary: The Iran war has sent fuel prices higher in Cambodia, squeezing families who rely on fishing and boats for their livelihoods. For children living on Tonle Sap, rising fuel costs pose yet another…

image.caption: For children living around Tonle Sap, access to education is increasingly under threat as an indirect consequence of rising fuel pricesImage: Action Education/Education Above All Foundation

blocks.text: Every morning, 12-year-old Soksan Set faces a journey most children his age never have to think about. Outside his home, there is no road, only water.

Soksan lives in Prek Toal, a floating community on Tonle Sap, Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lakewhere boats are the main means of transport. A Grade 4 student at the local primary school, he travels several kilometers on water to attend class and sometimes helps younger children along the way.

But increasingly, the biggest obstacle between Soksan and his classroom is not distance. It is fuel. His family, like many others in the commune, depends on fishing for their livelihood. When fuel prices rise, they are forced to make difficult choices.

"When gasoline prices go up, we don't have enough money to take our children to school regularly," said Soksan's father, 41-year-old Set Soeum. "We don't catch enough fish, and we need around three liters of gasoline a day to travel long distances for fishing. Because of this, Soksan often has to miss school."
For families living on the water, rising fuel costs can quickly become a barrier to education.

blocks.caption: Remote schools also depend on boats to transport teachers, textbooks, classroom materials, food and maintenance suppliesImage: Action Education/Education Above All Foundation

blocks.text: Why rising fuel costs hit Cambodia's poor the hardest

Cambodia relies heavily on imported fuel, leaving households exposed to global price shocks and regional supply disruptions. The 2026 Iran war has driven up energy costs, making transport to remote communities more expensive. Around Tonle Sap, this has hit students and their families.
Gasoline prices rose 45% and diesel prices more than 70% in March, the largest single-month increase since 2008, according to the World Bank.
Gasoline currently costs 5,700 riel ($1.41) per liter, up 26.7% from 4,500 riel ($1.11) a year ago, according to Global Petrol Prices.

Although Cambodia does not depend directly on the Strait of Hormuz for most of its fuel imports, it is exposed to higher global oil prices and supply disruptions affecting regional suppliers. Cambodia imports all of its petroleum products and has no domestic refining capacity.
For Soksan's family, the pressure is felt both on the fishing boat and the school boat. Some days, they borrow money to buy gasoline. Other days, they cut back on food, clothing or school supplies.

"Five students collect money to buy gasoline, sometimes just one liter at a time," Soksan said. When they cannot afford even that, they row themselves. "We row the boat ourselves. It can take up to an hour, but we still try to go to school," he noted.

On the Tonle Sap, 12-year-old Siyien Ly walks more than 30 minutes to school during the dry season. When flooding makes the roads impassable, she relies on an aid-supported school boat. Some of her classmates have stopped attending because their families cannot afford the cost of transport.
"Even though fuel prices are rising, we still keep trying to come to school because education is important for our future," Siyien said.
Siyien's family of six has four children in school. Her mother, Kunthea Chin, now sells sugarcane juice after Siyien's father developed serious hearing problems following a water-related accident.

Kunthea said that her daily income has fallen from about 80,000 riel ($20) to around 40,000 riel, while the cost of supplies has risen. The family spends around 600,000 riel ($150) a month on fuel, which they need for both the children's transport and her business.
Cambodia's floating schools face brunt of climate crisis
Taking risks to reach the classroom
Families also try to reduce costs by traveling together and sharing fuel expenses. Some have returned to traditional rowing boats. But saving money can come at the cost of safety.
When several children share a small boat, it can become crowded. During storms and heavy rain, parents worry about their children's safety on the water.
"My mother worries when too many students ride together," Siyien said.

Remote schools also depend on boats to transport teachers, textbooks, classroom materials, food and maintenance supplies. Higher fuel prices can therefore increase the cost of delivering education itself.

"For children living in floating and remote communities, access to education depends not only on having a school, but also on being able to reach it," said Samphors Vorn, country director of Action Education in Cambodia.

"When fuel prices rise, the cost of that journey rises with them. For families already living with very limited incomes, this can turn transportation into a barrier to attendance and, ultimately, to a child's right to education."
The Cambodian government has introduced measures to cushion consumers from international fuel-price increases, including fuel discounts, tax reductions and zero customs duties on fuel imports.
But subsidies at the pump cannot fully shield families whose incomes remain low and unpredictable.
Climate and economic shocks deepen education woes

Last year, DW reported from the region on how climate change was disrupting children's education. Rising and falling water levels, extreme weather and the dangers of traveling by boat were making it harder for children in floating communities to reach school.
The challenges have since deepened.

blocks.caption: Increasingly, the biggest obstacle between Soksan and his classroom is not distance, it is fuel.Image: Action Education/Education Above All Foundation

blocks.text: Today, 14-year-old Nary is no longer in the classroom. She has been unable to return because of persistent headaches following health complications linked to suspected long-term meningitis.
Her younger sister, 11-year-old Naren, continues to attend Grade 2. She relies on a school boat and pays around 500 riel ($0.12) for the return journey.

For their family, even small costs matter. Their father, Tit Sarin, earns around 30,000 riel ($7.50) a day from traditional fishing. But traveling farther across the lake to find fish can require about six liters of fuel, costing roughly $6.60.
"When we cannot afford fuel, we have to find other work," he said.
The family then works as day laborers, picking chilies for as little as 1,000 riel ($0.25) per kilogram. For families like Nary's, climate change and rising fuel costs are now a double burden.
Nary hopes to return to learning. Her father is saving to buy a boat dedicated to shuttling his children to school and back home.

articles.title: Cesafi 26: UC, USC lock horns in marquee men's basketball matchup
articles.summary: CEBU CITY, Philippines — A marquee matchup arrives early in the Cebu Schools Athletic Foundation, Inc. (Cesafi) Season 26 men’s basketball tournament as four-time finalist University of Cebu…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — A marquee matchup arrives early in the Cebu Schools Athletic Foundation, Inc. (Cesafi) Season 26 men’s basketball tournament as four-time finalist University of Cebu (UC) Webmasters clash with the University of San Carlos (USC) Warriors on Thursday, September 10, at the Cebu Coliseum.

The Warriors, coached by Paul Joven, made an early statement in the tournament by stunning four-time defending champion University of the Visayas (UV) Green Lancers, 81–68, on August 30 at the same venue.
The upset immediately raised questions about USC’s potential this season: are the Warriors emerging as a legitimate dark horse, or did the defending champions show some cracks in their armor?
Either way, USC has plenty of reasons for optimism.
UC-USC Cesafi 26 showdown

Veteran Jhoernel Tangkay, who returned to the team last season after his stint in the NCAA, delivered a strong performance against UV, while fully recovered big man Real Aureo also made his presence felt. But more than their individual performances, it was USC’s defense that proved decisive, forcing the Green Lancers into 20 turnovers.
Now, they face another major test against a UC squad that has become a regular fixture in the Cesafi finals.

The Webmasters, under lawyer and head coach Kern Sesante, are banking on a veteran-laden core that has battled UV in the championship series for four consecutive seasons. UC opened its Season 26 campaign with a convincing victory over newcomer and sister team University of Cebu Lapu-Lapu and Mandaue (UCLM) Webmasters on September 6.
Leading the charge is potential MVP candidate Ricofer Sordilla, complemented by dependable forward Luther Leonard and big men Charles Libatog and Carlo Salgarino.
UC’s depth could prove crucial against the Warriors, with Jepherson Nonol, Maverick Eligoyo, Arnold Minoza, and Danie Lapiz among the team’s other key pieces.
Adding an interesting subplot is former USC Warrior VJ Baruc, who is now serving as UC’s starting point guard.
UC recently announced that it had dropped and severed ties with former UV Baby Lancer Roderick Cambarijan after the player allegedly missed several weeks of practice.
The UC-USC showdown is scheduled for 7:45 p.m.
DBTC seeks second straight win
In the high school division, the Don Bosco Technical College (DBTC) Greywolves will look to make it two wins in a row when they face the San Carlos School of Cebu (SCSC) Baby Warriors at 6:15 p.m.
The Greywolves are coming off a dominant 70–49 victory over newcomer Paref Springdale School Titans last Sunday.
DBTC will try to carry that momentum into its next assignment against SCSC as it seeks another victory early in the Cesafi Season 26 campaign.

articles.title: Marcoleta insists on voting power as senator-judge despite detention
articles.summary: Senator Rodante Marcoleta insists that he still has a voting capacity as a senator-judge in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte despite being detained for plunder charges.

blocks.text: Published September 9, 2026 8:35pm
Senator Rodante Marcoleta insists that he still has a voting capacity as a senator-judge in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte despite being detained for plunder charges.
This was disclosed in a 16-page letter dated July 20 but released to the media on Wednesday, Marcoleta had written to Escudero and Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian while he was in detention.
“There is no impairment to my legal capacity to vote as a Senator-Judge for I am not under preventive suspension,” Marcoleta wrote.
Marcoleta maintains he was not issued a preventive suspension, neither has he resigned or incapacitated.

“I have been charged and arrested for the crime of Plunder on the basis of a politically-motivated administrative determination of probable cause by the Ombudsman. I have presented myself to the custody of the PNP- CIDG (Philippine National Police Criminal Investigation and Detection Group). However, these circumstances do not cause my office as Senator to be vacated,” Marcoleta said.

The detained senator also voiced his objection to Escudero as the presiding officer of Duterte’s impeachment, saying that it should be the Senate President. He said that the general rule applied that the Senate President, who oversees all Senate proceedings, should also preside over the trial.
The Senate should not distort the meaning of the Constitution, Marcoleta said.

Healso reiterated his support for the 16 vote threshold to convict Duterte, as this was already agreed upon when Escudero set the rules for the impeachment proceedings on July 3. Marcoleta was arrested three days later on July 6.
“For the foregoing reasons, I vote in favor of the ruling on the 16-vote requirement to convict the impeached Vice-President,” the lawmaker said.
Marcoleta is currently detained at the Quezon City Jail for plunder after he allegedly received P75 million in undeclared campaign donations. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: PNP beefs up deployment for BARMM polls to over 9,800 cops
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine National Police (PNP) increased its deployment to 9,821 police officers for security measures during the upcoming Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine National Police (PNP) increased its deployment to 9,821 police officers for security measures during the upcoming Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) parliamentary elections.
This was up from the 9,435 police officers the PNP previously said it was deploying.
In a statement on Wednesday, the PNP said the Police Regional Office (PRO) BARMM deployed 4,361 personnel, while other PROs deployed 2,430.

The law enforcement agency also said its Special Action Force deployed 830 officers; its Maritime Group deployed 250; the Explosive Ordnance Disposal and Canine Group deployed 146; and the Highway Patrol Group deployed 50.

Meanwhile, 1,754 of the PNP’s personnel were trained and deployed to serve on the Special Electoral Board (SEB), which is tapped when the commission’s personnel and local teachers could not oversee the polls.

Apart from the SEB, the national police force noted that 4,313 of the deployed personnel will be stationed at voting centers across BARMM, while 856 will man checkpoints, 218 will monitor local treasurers’ offices, and 208 will secure local Commission on Elections (Comelec) offices.
Further, the PNP detailed that 2,120 officers were deployed to stand by as quick reaction forces, and 352 as civil disturbance management.

“Our personnel are deployed not only to secure election areas, but to help create an environment where people can exercise their right to vote freely, peacefully, and without intimidation,” PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. said in the statement.
“Ang bawat botante ay dapat makaboto nang ligtas at malaya. Makipagtulungan tayo at agad ireport ang anumang kahina-hinalang gawain sa mga awtoridad,” he added.
(Each voter should be able to vote safely and freely. Let us work together and report whatever suspicious activities we see to the authorities.)
Some 2.393 million registered voters are expected to troop to 5,212 voting precincts across BARMM to fill 78 seats in the autonomous region’s parliament this coming Monday, Sept. 14. /mcm

articles.title: For GCash’s early private equity backers, record IPO will be ultimate payday
articles.summary: GCash's blockbuster IPO could turn years of paper gains into billions for its early private equity backers. For the retail investors buying in now, the question is how much growth still remains.

blocks.text: GCash's blockbuster IPO could turn years of paper gains into billions for its early private equity backers. For the retail investors buying in now, the question is how much growth still remains.

items: GCash is preparing for an initial public offering (IPO) that could be the largest in Philippine history, allowing ordinary investors to participate in its success and providing early backers with a significant exit opportunity.

The IPO will involve the issuance of up to 1.61 billion new shares and the sale of 6.42 billion shares from existing shareholders, with 80% of the shares being secondary, indicating that most proceeds will benefit early investors rather than raising new capital.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

GCash has become so ubiquitous that its blue QR codes are just as easy to find in sari-sari stores as they are in malls. Its upcoming initial public offering (IPO) now promises to give ordinary investors a chance to own a piece of that success.
And for some of GCash’s earliest financial backers, an IPO poised to become the largest in Philippine history also offers the kind of exit private equity (PE) investors spend years hoping for.

Bow Wave Capital, Warburg Pincus, Insight Partners, and LGVP invested in Mynt — the parent company of the e-wallet giant — long before it commanded anything close to the valuation it’s seeking today. They helped bankroll its rise from fast-growing fintech to profitable household name. Now, the IPO could allow them to turn what has so far been paper gains into cash.
And this is no small liquidity event.

Under the latest offer structure, Mynt will issue up to 1.61 billion new shares, while existing shareholders will sell up to 6.42 billion shares. Another 1.20 billion shares available under the overallotment option will also come from existing owners.

That means only 20% of the firm offer is primary, while 80% is secondary. In other words, most of the shares being sold will come from existing shareholders rather than from new shares issued to raise fresh capital for Mynt.

By the time the bell rings, the vast majority of the IPO proceeds will be going to shareholders selling down stakes accumulated years earlier, giving some of GCash’s earliest backers the ultimate payday.
The institutional sellers are mostly early financial investors. At the P10 ceiling and assuming the overallotment option is fully exercised, the prospectus shows:

items: Bow Wave Capital, through ASP Philippines – could sell about P27.04 billion worth of shares, cutting its stake from 6% to around 1.82%
Warburg Pincus, through Lion Fintech Investments – could sell around P12.18 billion, bringing its stake down from 2.70% to around 0.82%
Insight Partners, through Insight PHP Holdings – could sell about P8.53 billion, reducing its stake from 1.89% to around 0.57%
Advanced New Technologies, an Ant International-linked company – could sell about P25.18 billion, reducing its stake from 6.22% to around 2.30%
LGVP, through its three investment vehicles – could sell around P2.66 billion combined, cutting their combined stake from about 0.59% to roughly 0.18%

blocks.text: These are investors deeply familiar with fintech.

Bow Wave is a relatively specialized private equity fund whose mandate centers on online and mobile payments. It first backed Mynt in 2020, when GCash’s pandemic-era growth was taking off and Mynt was valued at close to US$1 billion, meaning it has been invested for around six years. Bow Wave has also backed Ascend Money, the company behind Thailand’s TrueMoney Wallet, another Southeast Asian digital payments success story.

Warburg Pincus, meanwhile, is one of the world’s most prominent private equity firms and has plenty of experience betting on digital finance in emerging Asian markets. Its portfolio has included MoMo, Vietnam’s largest e-wallet, Indonesia’s GoTo Group, which combines Gojek, Tokopedia and GoTo Financial, and Advance Intelligence Group, whose businesses include buy-now-pay-later platform Atome. Warburg joined Mynt’s 2021 funding round, giving it roughly a five-year holding period by the time of the planned IPO.

Insight Partners came into Mynt in the same 2021 round. The New York growth investor has an extensive fintech portfolio that includes payments company Checkout.com, digital bank N26, Indonesian payments firm Xendit, Flutterwave, and financial infrastructure company Tink.

blocks.caption: [Finterest] GCash, Maya IPOs in 2026? What this means for potential investors

blocks.text: But the sell-down doesn’t mean GCash’s most important strategic owners are heading for the exits. Globe Capital Venture Holdings, Mynt’s single biggest shareholder at 33.84%, along with Ant International Technologies (21.44%), Ayala-Mitsubishi vehicle AM 50 Ventures (13.02%), and MUFG Bank (8.05%), are all staying put.
Nor should the PE (private equity) sell-down automatically be read as a vote of no confidence in GCash.

“It is fair to say that the IPO provides a liquidity or partial exit opportunity,” FirstMetroSec vice president and digital solutions and investor engagement division head Andoy Beltran told Rappler, adding, “but I would be careful about interpreting that as them losing confidence in GCash because those are two very different things.”

After all, exiting is part of the private equity playbook. Unlike strategic investors such as Globe or Ayala, PE and growth funds generally don’t buy stakes with the intention of holding them indefinitely. They invest, help a company scale and multiply in value, then eventually sell some or all of their stakes so they can return capital and profits to their own investors.

The timing is hardly unusual either. Recall Bow Wave first invested around 2020, while Warburg Pincus and Insight came in during 2021, putting them at roughly five to six years in Mynt by the time of the IPO. From my own experience consulting on private equity deals — including fintech investments — that’s the exit window that funds look for.
That may be the more important question for retail investors taking their place.

GCash is already operating at enormous scale. Mynt posted P79.7 billion in adjusted revenue and P17.25 billion in net income in 2025, while GCash reached 41.5 million monthly active users by June 2026, equivalent to nearly 56% of Filipino adults.

Growth, however, has cooled from its earlier breakneck pace. Adjusted revenue in H1 2026 only rose 9.8%, while net income grew 7.3%. DragonFi equity analyst Jarrod Tin argues that GCash has already deeply penetrated its core wallet market, with competition from Maya, MariBank, and other financial apps making the next leg harder.
However, Beltran still sees a growth story, with more runway in lending, savings, investments and other financial services, but cautions investors not to expect the old growth rates indefinitely.
“The question is how much of that future growth is already being priced into the IPO,” he said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: EU proposes more restrictions for Airbnb, holiday rentals
articles.summary: The European Union wants tighter rules on short-term rentals to tackle housing shortages in tourist hotspots.

image.caption: Protesters in Malaga call for Airbnb to be 'out of our neighborhoods' [FILE: June 2024]Image: JORGE GUERRERO/AFP

blocks.text: Airbnb and other companies providing short-term home rentals could face tighter restrictions after the European Commission proposed new rules on Wednesday to help tackle housing shortages in tourist hotspots.

A surge in short-term holiday rentals has contributed to a shortage of affordable housing and a spike in housing prices in many of Europe's most popular tourist destinations, prompting residents to protest in recent years .
What do we know about the EU's affordable housing proposal?

The EU's executive branch unveiled the measures as part of an "affordable housing" package, which will allow local authorities to limit short-term rentals to address what European Commission vice-president Teresa Ribera described as a "terrible crisis."
"When the market fails to deliver something as fundamental as an affordable home, public authorities have a responsibility to act," the Spanish politician said.

The measures seek to harmonize rules across the bloc, after attempts to crack down on Airbnb-style rentals by authorities in cities such as Paris, Berlin and Barcelona, among others, were met with legal challenges by rental and tourism companies.

The European Commission's Affordable Housing Act — which still needs to be approved by EU legislators and EU member states — would provide cities with legal support by clarifying when local authorities can act against housing companies without breaking EU single market rules.

Under the proposal, city and local authorities would be allowed to limit short-term and holiday rentals as well as curb the purchase of property for short-term letting in areas considered to be "under housing stress," the European Commission said.
Spain: Tourism boom worsens housing crisis
For an area to be defined as "under stress," certain parameters — including the ratio between local housing prices and incomes — would have to be met.
Before restrictions can be introduced, cities would have to show that holiday rentals have had a major negative impact on the affordability or availability of housing for at least three years.
The proposed legislation will not impact landlords renting out their primary residence for short-term periods.
The Commission also recommended that authorities free up land for more housing and modernize planning and construction of new homes to address housing shortages.
How have rental companies reacted?
CCIA Europe, a lobbying group that represents Airbnb, among others, said the EU's measures fail to address the need for independent assessment of the restrictions.

"Europe will not solve its housing crisis by giving cities an EU framework to restrict short-term rentals and then letting them police their own ​compliance," CCIA's head of ⁠policy Alexandre Roure said in a statement.

"Without independent scrutiny or effective redress, this proposal will remain a paper tiger, leaving disproportionate restrictions ⁠in place and undermining ​the legal certainty the Affordable Housing Act is meant to provide," Roure added.

articles.title: PDP-Laban: Lowering 16-vote threshold for conviction violates Constitution
articles.summary: The PDP led by its president Baste Duterte said Wednesday that the lowering the existing 16-vote threshold for a conviction in the Senate impeachment court will violate the Constitution.

blocks.text: Published September 9, 2026 8:18pm

The Partido Demokratiko Pilipino (PDP)—led by its president, acting Davao City Mayor Sebastian "Baste" Duterte—said Wednesday that the lowering the existing 16-vote threshold for a conviction in the Senate impeachment court would violate the Constitution.

The party issued the statement a day after the possibility of lowering the threshold was raised during Day 23 of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, sister of Sebastian, since four of the 24 Senators are not participating in the ongoing proceedings.

Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta are detained on separate plunder charges, while Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa is in hiding amid an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court.
Senator Loren Legarda, meanwhile, has not been attending the trial for weeks now due to health concerns, specifically a lung problem that she is having treated overseas.

“(PDP-LABAN) views with great alarm, the efforts of certain members of the Senate to once again bend the law to the breaking point, by attempting to tamper with the evident intent of the framers of the Constitution in setting a threshold of 16 votes of all the members of the Senate, in order to convict an impeachable officer, in order to stave off the acquittal of a Vice-President due to weak evidence and a less than competent prosecution panel,” lawyer Ferdinand Topacio, PDP-Laban national spokesman, said in a statement.

“The Constitution is a sacred document that should be placed above the swirling winds of political expediency. The yardstick of sixteen was specifically formulated to insulate the Senate, sitting as an Impeachment Court, from political manipulation and interference, such as what is happening now,” Topacio added.
Topacio said the 16-vote threshold is an “immovable standard” supported by debates in the Constitutional Commission and by ruling case law.

“The present administration, with its evil plan of lowering the threshold, is showing its panic and desperation in the face of the impending defeat of its vile efforts to unseat and disqualify the clear choice of the people for Vice-President and for President in 2028,” he said. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: College students can get a year of Google AI Plus for free
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – Google is offering college students in the Philippines a one-year free subscription to Google’s AI Plus Plan. Google AI Plus includes Study Notebooks, direct access to Gemini…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Google is offering college students in the Philippines a one-year free subscription to Google’s AI Plus Plan.
Google AI Plus includes Study Notebooks, direct access to Gemini Omni, a personalized Daily Brief, Gemini Live, and 400 GB of cloud storage across Google Drive, Gmail, and Google Photos.

With Study Notebooks, students can upload their class materials to have Gemini create a step-by-step study plan. Guides and practice tests can be generated while important dates like exams and deadlines will directly be integrated into Google Calendar.

Meanwhile, Gemini’s interactive visualizations can help students generate 3d simulations to further understand topics. This can range from visual understanding of tables or grids for various math problems, science topics, and more.

How to avail the plan

articles.title: Liz Truss to relaunch podcast on channel of broadcaster famous for ‘grow concrete’ exchange
articles.summary:
Podcast will be on YouTube site of Mike Graham, fired from TalkTV after racist post appeared on his Facebook page

When Liz Truss launched her podcast last year, she

blocks.text: When Liz Truss launched her podcast last year, she declared it would bring a “counter-revolution” to take on the “deep state”, which, she said, “tried to destroy” her.

The revolution, however, has not yet arrived. Truss, whose stint as UK prime minister abruptly ended after her disastrous mini-budget crashed the economy, has so far failed to find a wide audience in her media career.
Her podcast episodes hosted on YouTube often receive fewer than 4,000 views each, which is understood to be below the amount generally needed to monetise a video.
Now, Truss is relaunching her podcast and joining the former TalkTV host Mike Graham’s YouTube channel, UKLive, where she will be livestreaming twice a week.

Graham was dismissed from Rupert Murdoch’s digital channel after the company said he had failed to cooperate with an investigation into a racist post that appeared on his Facebook account. The post inquired: “Why are we surrounded by non-white people?” Graham claimed he did not post it and that he was hacked.

The presenter, whose new channel calls itself “the home of common sense”, came to public prominence after claiming on air that it was possible to grow concrete. Graham was questioning the eco-activist and carpenter Cameron Ford on whether timber was a sustainable building material. Cameron said timber was “regenerative”, adding: “You can grow trees. You can’t grow concrete.” Graham replied: “Yeah, you can.”

blocks.caption: The former TalkTV presenter Mike Graham. Photograph: Andrew Stehrenberger/Alamy

blocks.text: Graham’s channel does generate income, securing enough views to qualify for YouTube’s scheme that shares ad revenue with creators. While UKLive only averages about 24,000 views a video, its prolific output of 1,700 posts in the last year means it has secured 41m views in that time, according to the Socialpruf analytics site. That is enough to generate thousands of pounds a month in ad revenue.

The rise of YouTube has created a home for those shunned by mainstream outlets, but its growth has also in effect created a whole world of broadcasting outside of the regulated world of mainstream TV.

“Since Ofcom took over broadcast regulation in 2003, the way we watch television has changed beyond recognition,” said Chris Banatvala, who was Ofcom’s founding director of standards. “We now have a huge range of content that looks and feels like television – and is often available on the same television set – but isn’t subject to the same standards.
“Viewers may have no idea whether what they are watching is regulated by Ofcom or not – and these regulatory grey areas are only likely to grow.

“It is a good thing that the public has access to such a wide range of views and content. But the law has not kept pace, parliament has yet to confront the implications of this increasingly blurred distinction, and the platforms themselves have not always proved able to prevent serious harm.”
after newsletter promotion

Truss will be joining a host of other presenters including the former actor Laurence Fox, who was suspended from GB News after making sexualised comments on air about a female journalist. Also on the roster is Mark Littlewood, a former director of the Institute of Economic Affairs thinktank, which praised many of Truss’s economic policies, and the pro-Reform commentator Ellie Hodges.

Truss may hope to benefit from Graham’s larger following; his channel has 179,000 subscribers compared with her 32,300. Recent podcasts from Truss include one in which the commentator June Slater claimed “Labour is panicking as Reform surges in Makerfield byelection”. Andy Burnham won for Labour in Makerfield by a wide margin.

Another is an interview with Lucy Connolly in which she complains she was “jailed for a tweet”. Connolly was sent to prison in 2024 for stirring up racial hatred against asylum seekers in a post in which she called for asylum hotels to be burned down.

The former prime minister said her new show would have “exciting new guests”. Truss has been attempting to relaunch her career in recent months, including setting up a new private members’ club in Mayfair with the property tycoon Robert Tchenguiz.
The club, named the Leconfield, states on its website that it is a “beacon of sophistication and refined elegance” that has “curated an exclusive sanctuary where tradition meets contemporary luxury”.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz says 'I leave with a smile' after epic US Open loss
articles.summary: NEW YORK — At the end, when five riveting sets and one agonizingly tight tiebreak were over — and when the latest-finishing match in U.S. Open history had concluded — Ben Shelton was not the only…

blocks.text: Carlos Alcaraz, of Spain, acknowledges the fans after losing to Ben Shelton, of the United States, in the quarterfinal round of the U.S. Open tennis championships, early Wednesday, Sept. 9, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Adam Hunger)

NEW YORK — At the end, when five riveting sets and one agonizingly tight tiebreak were over — and when the latest-finishing match in U.S. Open history had concluded — Ben Shelton was not the only player smiling.
Carlos Alcaraz, the player Shelton had just defeated in an entertaining, spine-tingling marathon, was smiling too.

The dethroned defending champ grinned as he walked to the net to hug Shelton. And he did so again a few minutes later when he stood in a hallway surrounded by reporters, reflecting on a night that seemed to have taken every ounce of his strength to endure.
“I leave the court happy,” Alcaraz said. “I leave the court with a smile. I am proud of myself, how I fought.”
There was probably not a single person in Arthur Ashe Stadium who would have disagreed.

Though many of the thousands of fans who remained until the 3:33 a.m. conclusion – yes, you read that time right – cheered for Shelton, the top-ranked American who now meets compatriot Frances Tiafoe in the semis, there were plenty who cheered for Alcaraz, one of the most charismatic players of his or any generation, and one of the most naturally gifted players ever born.

blocks.caption: Ben Shelton, right, of the United States, is congratulated by Carlos Alcaraz, of Spain, after winning their match in the quarterfinal round of the U.S. Open tennis championships, Wednesday, Sept. 9, 2026, in New York.

blocks.text: Ben Shelton, right, of the United States, is congratulated by Carlos Alcaraz, of Spain, after winning their match in the quarterfinal round of the U.S. Open tennis championships, Wednesday, Sept. 9, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Heather Khalifa)
“Ole, Ole Ole Ole,” Alcaraz’s fans chanted, and “Vamos Carlos!” — competing with shouts of “USA, USA” or just “Let’s Go Ben!”
Most importantly, Alcaraz said he was leaving healthy. That had been a real concern going into this U.S. Open after a four-month break due to a wrist injury.
“As I said before the tournament began, my expectation was to go there, compete, play these kind of matches, be healthy,” he said after his 6-7 (5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6 (10-7) defeat.
“I mean it was close, it really was close, so I was disappointed I didn’t get the win in the end, but I’m just happy … physically I was really tired, but I found a way to push myself.”
The Spaniard also had nothing but praise for Shelton, who played the match of his young career to defeat the seven-time Grand Slam champion.

“Shelton played a very complete, very mature match,” Alcaraz said in Spanish. “He knew exactly what to do at every moment. And, physically, he’s a beast. It seemed like he had no weaknesses whatsoever. “
“It was a war,” Shelton said. “Carlos is one of the greatest champions of our sport. It was the most enjoyable match I’ve had in my career, for sure.”
Alcaraz had arrived at the U.S. Open with much uncertainty as to how much of a liability his wrist injury remained.
But he seemed healthy from the start, and said he felt better than expected. In his first four rounds he lost only one set.

“It feels like I’ve been competing the whole time,” he said of his extended break. “I surprise myself the way that I’m feeling, and the way that I’m recovering after every match. I’m just really happy about it,” he had said after advancing to the fourth round, “that I’m able to perform at my best after every match.”

Alcaraz also said he’d be taking more long breaks in the future, since he didn’t need to depend on a rhythm or to play a lot of tournaments. And he was so relaxed, he didn’t even know, after handily defeating Tommy Paul in his fourth-round match, who he’d be facing next. Former U.S. Open champ Andy Roddick, a commentator for ESPN, let him know.

Then came Tuesday’s (and Wednesday’s) quarterfinals, and Shelton. After Alcaraz won the first, tight set, Shelton started playing out of his mind. He took the next two sets. Alcaraz rallied for the fourth, and then the two traded games in a nerve-wracking fifth.

Among those in the crowd cheering for Alcaraz were Anushka Sancheti and Prajakti Kapde. The two friends, both 28, had traveled to attend together — Sancheti from Atlanta, and Kapde from Raleigh, North Carolina.
The two are Alcaraz supporters, and yet, they’d not only never seen him play in person — they’d never been to a professional tennis match.

They’d bought their tickets not knowing who would be playing. And, somehow, they managed to see not only their favorite player, but their favorite player in a match that will surely be talked about for years to come. Both for the record it broke, and for the incredible fight it featured, between two extraordinary 23-year olds.
“We do understand how historic this is,” Sancheti said.
Added Kapde: “We really can’t believe it!”

articles.title: Oil prices rise as Brent crude exceeds $100
articles.summary: ISTANBUL – Oil prices climbed 2.2 percent on Wednesday, with Brent crude futures riding above USD100 a barrel as escalating US-Iran tensions continued to roil global energy markets. The…

blocks.text: ISTANBUL – Oil prices climbed 2.2 percent on Wednesday, with Brent crude futures riding above USD100 a barrel as escalating US-Iran tensions continued to roil global energy markets.
The international benchmark surpassed the USD100-a-barrel threshold as of 0730 GMT, extending gains amid heightened concerns over potential disruptions to oil supplies.
The price of West Texas Intermediate (WTI) also rose 1.5 percent to USD94.5 per barrel.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Wednesday its naval forces targeted two US vessels and eight oil tankers in the Persian Gulf, claiming the attacks inflicted heavy damage on the vessels.
In a statement, the IRGC said the strikes were “carried out in response to US aggression, including an attack on five Iranian oil tankers in the Persian Gulf.”
The IRGC did not identify the US vessels or oil tankers it said were targeted, nor did it provide details on when the attacks took place.

The statement also said Iranian naval forces had targeted 10 other vessels that “attempted to enter a restricted and unsafe area of the Strait of Hormuz,” claiming they were acting with the “encouragement and support of the US military.”

The two countries signed a memorandum of understanding in June, mediated by Pakistan and Qatar, outlining steps toward ending hostilities, reopening the Strait of Hormuz, and addressing economic restrictions.

The two sides have since accused each other of failing to implement commitments under the memorandum, while military tensions have continued alongside disputes over sanctions and navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. (Anadolu)

articles.title: Mandaue City strengthens its mental health awareness campaign
articles.summary: MANDAUE CITY, Cebu — The Mandaue City Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Office is strengthening its mental health awareness campaign in schools and barangays. Niño Krisbayani Dargantes,…

blocks.text: MANDAUE CITY, Cebu — The Mandaue City Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Office is strengthening its mental health awareness campaign in schools and barangays.

Niño Krisbayani Dargantes, officer-in-charge of the office, said they regularly coordinate with the Department of Education-Mandaue, which refers mental health-related concerns involving students to their office.
Students experiencing mental health problems may be referred to the office for assessment by psychometricians.
Psychometricians will initially assess the students and refer those who need further intervention to a psychologist or psychiatrist.
Dargantes said the office has been conducting mental health advocacy activities in both public and private schools, as well as in barangays.

“Naa naman sa schools ron. Nagconduct nami og advocacies like [sa] St. Joseph private and public,” said Dargantes. (It is in schools now. We are conducting advocacies in, like, St. Joseph private and public.)
More mental health programs in Mandaue
The office is also coordinating with the Department of Education and parent-teacher associations for additional mental health orientations for parents and teachers.
Dargantes said teachers and parents play an important role in identifying changes in a child’s behavior that may indicate an underlying mental health concern.
He said some behavioral changes are often dismissed as normal or temporary, which could result in signs of distress being overlooked.

Meanwhile, Dargantes said there is still no schedule for the conduct of safety drills in city schools. He said there have been concerns about the possible impact of the activity on students’ mental health.
Dargantes cited a statement from the Psychological Association of the Philippines raising concerns that such drills could cause trauma among students.///

articles.title: Renewed U.S.-Iran exchanges send oil price back over $100 US for first time in several weeks
articles.summary: Iran said Wednesday it had attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the U.S. sank five Iranian oil tankers, with the attacks ‌in and around the vital waterway sending the international Brent…

image.caption: Vessels at the Strait of Hormuz, as seen from Musandam, Oman, are shown on Sunday. (Reuters)

blocks.text: World

Iran said Wednesday it had attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the U.S. sank five Iranian oil tankers, with the attacks ‌in and around the vital waterway sending the international Brent crude benchmark over $100 US a barrel for the first time since July.
In addition to attacks on the war, Iran fired missiles at base used by U.S. in Jordan

Iran said Wednesday it had attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the U.S. sank five Iranian oil tankers, in the biggest declared wave of tit-for-tat attacks on shipping by both sides since the start of the six-month-old war.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it had responded with a ballistic missile attack on a base used by U.S. forces near Al Azraq, in eastern Jordan, and had fired on two U.S. vessels and eight oil tankers attempting ⁠to cross an area of the Strait of Hormuz that it has declared off limits.

The attacks ‌in and around the vital waterway sent the price of oil surging, with the international Brent crude benchmark breaching $100 US a barrel for the first time since July. Since the war began, oil prices have been as low as $70, reflecting since-scuppered hopes that the U.S. and Iran would agree on a plan that would allow stranded tankers to move oil out of the Persian Gulf safely.

Escalating combat between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-aligned Houthis that control most populated parts of Yemen has created additional uncertainty for energy markets. On Tuesday, the ​Houthis launched an attack on four cities in Saudi ⁠Arabia, causing huge fires at oil installations that were visible from space. Saudi authorities said 73 people were wounded.

American consumers have felt the pinch at the gas pumps, a politically sensitive issue with less than two months before November midterm elections that threaten Republican control of the Senate and House of Representatives.

A gallon of regular gasoline averaged $4.15 in the U.S. on Tuesday, up 26 per cent from a year ago, according to motor club AAA. Diesel, at $5.90 a gallon, cost 59 per cent more than the same day a year earlier.

"In our view, reaching a durable deal before the U.S. midterm elections is increasingly unlikely, and it could remain elusive even beyond that," Bank of America analysts said in a Tuesday research note.

Average gas prices across Canada have also climbed since the start of the war, with increases between 25 and 40 per cent in most locations. The federal government announced an extension of the gas tax holiday as a result, until the end of January.
Iran reveals area of restricted maritime zone

The Americans said they destroyed five Iranian oil tankers overnight, releasing video of ships ablaze before they sank. The U.S. military's Central Command called its attacks a response to the IRGC targeting a U.S. Navy warship twice with ballistic missiles over the previous two days.

"Iran continues to try to hit U.S. naval ships, and for every time they do that or try to do that, they're going to lose tankers," U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters during a visit to Colombia.
Iran says it is imposing a wider off-limits zone around the strait ‌and using new, more capable missiles to attack U.S. ships.
Can Iran really launch sea mines from rockets? | About That

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Wednesday a ‌maritime restricted area would extend ​from Chabahar in Iran ​into parts of the Gulf ​of Oman and ⁠the ⁠Arabian Sea, ‌with its precise co-ordinates to be announced. The announcement ⁠follows comments Sunday by ‌Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, who was ​quoted by ⁠state media as ⁠saying Iran would soon ⁠establish ⁠a restricted ​zone outside the Strait ​of ⁠Hormuz.

Meanwhile, a tanker carrying about two million barrels of Iraqi fuel oil was struck by a ‌drone in Iraqi territorial waters on Wednesday, two Iraqi port officials told Reuters. It caused a fire aboard the Panama-flagged oil tanker New Andros, the port officials said, but there were no reports of casualties among the 22 crew members.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency had said earlier that vessels in the northern ⁠Gulf and Gulf of Oman were hit by disabling fire during military activity in the region overnight.
Iran has also threatened oil tankers in Kuwaiti and Bahraini ports, according to a statement carried by state media.
Iran has largely choked off transit through the Strait of Hormuz that carried one-fifth of global oil before the war, as well as significant amounts of natural gas, fertilizer and other resources.

Washington has responded with a military blockade of Iranian ports, and says it has been able to ​guide many tankers through the strait, although independent monitors say the extent to which oil is escaping has become increasingly difficult to assess.

items: Iran-backed Houthis attack Saudi oil facilities, injuring dozens
Iran says it will announce new Strait of Hormuz 'exclusion zone'

blocks.text: Preliminary data showed just six ships crossing with transponders over the last 24 hours.
Iran also said it had fired ballistic missiles at a base used by U.S. forces in Jordan.
Iran said that its missiles fired inflicted ⁠heavy damage, while Jordan said its air defences had intercepted 18 of the 20 Iranian missiles, with two falling in unpopulated areas and no casualties.
Video filmed in Ash-Shajarah, in northern Jordan, and verified by Reuters showed flashes lighting up the night sky.
Iran has targeted U.S. bases in ⁠the region ⁠throughout the war and killed at least two U.S. military personnel in ​a strike on Jordan in July.

articles.title: BIR clears VAT refunds for exporters before certification
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) has allowed qualified export-oriented enterprises (EOEs) to claim refunds for value-added tax (VAT) paid while awaiting zero-rating…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) has allowed qualified export-oriented enterprises (EOEs) to claim refunds for value-added tax (VAT) paid while awaiting zero-rating certification from the Department of Trade and Industry under transition rules that ran until the end of 2025.

Under Revenue Memorandum Circular No. 096-2026, the BIR said EOEs may seek refunds for VAT paid on local purchases and importations from Nov. 28, 2024, the effectivity of the CREATE MORE Act, until the issuance of their VAT zero-rating certifications.
Also, the DTI-Export Marketing Bureau (DTI-EMB) will allow the refund if it issues the certification during the transitory period, which runs from Nov. 28, 2024, to Dec. 31, 2025.
Meanwhile, the BIR had already issued a circular in April 2025 defining eased procedures and requirements for VAT refund claims.

But the latest issuance clarifies the refund period amid differences in the dates when EOEs received their zero-rating certifications, which left some qualified enterprises continuing to pay VAT after the CREATE MORE Act took effect.

“Export-oriented enterprises received their VAT zero-rating certifications on different dates during the transition period.We are clarifying how qualified export-oriented enterprises should treat the VAT incurred during the processing of these certifications, ensuring they have a clear basis for their refund claims.” BIR Commissioner Charlito Martin R. Mendoza said.
“Our objective is to ensure fair and consistent tax treatment for qualified export-oriented enterprises during the transition to the new zero-rating certification system,” he added.
Likewise, the circular clarified EOEs that met the 70-percent export threshold last year but lacked the DTI-EMB certification will lose their VAT refund entitlement for the following year.
Additionally, they may instead carry forward unused input VAT to following taxable quarters and use it against future VAT liabilities, subject to existing tax rules.
Meanwhile, the BIR also said that taxpayers cannot receive a VAT refund if they have already refunded, credited, adjusted, recovered it from suppliers, or otherwise used it.
Effective April 1, 2025, businesses may file VAT refund claims covering pre-CREATE MORE periods without DTI-EMB certification. /pai

articles.title: German chancellor accuses far-right AfD party of seeking ‘ethnic cleansing’
articles.summary: Friedrich Merz says Alternative für Deutschland is ‘dividing our society’ after party won nearly 44% of vote in Saxony-Anhalt state election

blocks.text: Germany’s chancellor, Friedrich Merz, has accused the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) of seeking “ethnic cleansing” with its “remigration” drive, after the nativist party’s seismic weekend victory in a state election.

In his first public confrontation with the AfD since Sunday’s shock outcome in Saxony-Anhalt, Merz said at a raucous parliamentary debate that the far-right party would take an axe to one of the pillars of the German economy with a racist campaign of mass deportations.
“The term ‘remigration’ is nothing but a synonym for ethnic cleansing based on origin and skin colour,” he said on Wednesday to applause from the other parties in the Bundestag lower house.
In a fiery speech addressed to the AfD parliamentary group, which repeatedly interrupted him with loud taunts and heckling, Merz said millions of working immigrants were crucial to German society.

“If those working in Germany have to leave the country again because you are championing ‘remigration’,” Merz said, “then the skilled trades in Germany will no longer be able to function: not a single care home will remain open, not a single hospital in Germany will remain operational, and not a single restaurant in Germany will be able to stay in business.”
He said the AfD’s rhetoric, which propelled it to the strongest showing for a far-right party in a German state since the Nazi period, “is precisely what is dividing our society so deeply”.

Support for Merz, a conservative Christian Democrat, has plummeted in the 16 months since he took office at the helm of a coalition with the centre-left Social Democrats, amid disappointment over slow progress on economic growth and the cost of living.
He has adopted a hard line on border policy in a faltering bid to win back AfD supporters, and acknowledged Germany still had “problems in the area of migration”.
“We still have many people in Germany who should not have permanent residency. This is consensus in the [ruling] coalition, that we need to deport more people,” he said on Wednesday.

“But we make a careful distinction between those who work in Germany, who contribute to our prosperity, and who are welcome here, and those who do not have permanent residency in Germany and who must leave our country. Unlike you [the AfD], we take great care to make this distinction.”

blocks.caption: (From l to r) AfD party co-chair Tino Chrupalla, Ulrich Siegmund and Alice Weidel a day after the Saxony-Anhalt state election. Photograph: Clemens Bilan/EPA

blocks.text: The AfD won nearly 44% of the vote in Saxony-Anhalt but fell three seats short of an absolute majority. Its chief candidate, Ulrich Siegmund, is seeking potential supporters among the other parties to elect him as state premier.
after newsletter promotion

Merz, who has acknowledged that his unpopularity played a role in the halving of support for his party in the state, tried to put a brave face on the rout. “Fifty-six percent of voters in Saxony-Anhalt didn’t vote for you,” he told the AfD.

He accused Siegmund, whose party is classed as rightwing extremist by domestic intelligence, of “electoral fraud” by already breaking a campaign promise not to seek to govern the state if he failed to win an absolute majority.
“And you won’t manage that in Germany either” at the federal level, Merz told the AfD co-leader Alice Weidel. “Nowhere in Germany will you get a majority. You are and remain a destructive force.”

Merz also attacked the AfD for its opposition to military assistance for Ukraine, and accused it of making common cause with Russia, which Berlin has alleged is mounting a sabotage and disinformation campaign on its soil.

He said that despite “clear evidence” a failed drone bomb attack at Leipzig airport last month “had been planned in Russia for months and was specifically directed against Germany”, the AfD had remained silent on it.
Earlier from the podium, Weidel savoured her party’s resounding election victory, saying the CDU had been “pulverised” and calling it a referendum on Merz’s leadership.

Attacking the government’s migration policy and blaming it for crime and other security problems, Weidel said: “Your time is up. The public want a change in policy, and they will get it,” reiterating her party’s aim to form a federal government in the foreseeable future.
Polls show Merz’s fractious coalition would not have a majority in a general election, which is not scheduled until 2029.
The AfD is polling in first place at 28% to 29%, with the wind at its back before another two state polls this month, in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.

articles.title: Sherwin Gatchalian: Court to decide Marcoleta, Estrada impeachment attendance
articles.summary: Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian on Wednesday said detained senators Rodante Marcoleta and Jinggoy Estrada would have to seek permission from the Sandiganbayan to attend Senate sessions, including…

blocks.text: Published September 9, 2026 7:49pm

Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian on Wednesday said detained senators Rodante Marcoleta and Jinggoy Estrada would have to seek permission from the Sandiganbayan to attend Senate sessions, including the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.
In an interview with reporters, however, Gatchalian said both senators are in the custody of the courts.
"By process, they will have to ask permission there if they can attend the session or the impeachment. In the past, it was like that,” Gatchalian said.
Asked if he would write to the Sandiganbayan, Gatchalian said the senators themselves would have to ask for permission.
“So, the court will decide if there is justification for them to attend even a session or the impeachment,” Gatchalian said.

Estrada and Marcoleta are currently detained over plunder charges. Marcoleta has reportedly written to Gatchalian and impeachment presiding officer Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero, saying there was no impairment to his capacity to serve as a senator-judge.
Estrada, however, has already petitioned the Sandiganbayan to allow him to attend the impeachment trial. The anti-graft court denied the plea for lack of merit.
In July, Marcoleta also publicly asked the Senate to find ways to allow him and Estrada to participate in the impeachment trial.
Marcoleta’s request was again raised when the Senate impeachment court discussed the voting threshold for convicting Duterte.
With four senators unable to attend the impeachment proceedings, questions were raised over how many votes would be needed to convict her.
The Senate impeachment court is set to consult legal experts on the matter through amici curiae.

Aside from Estrada and Marcoleta, Sen. Dela Rosa has also been unable to attend the proceedings as he remains in hiding amid an ICC arrest warrant over alleged crimes against humanity linked to the Duterte administration’s drug war.
Legarda, meanwhile, has missed the proceedings after leaving the country and has sought an extended absence, reportedly due to health reasons.— MCG, GMA News

blocks.text: Jollibee is marking a milestone with its global collaboration with DreamWorks Animation for the worldwide theatrical release of Forgotten Island on September 23, 2026.

blocks.caption: Jollibee Forgotten Island BINI

blocks.text: At the heart of Forgotten Island are lifelong best friends Jo and Raissa, who discover a mysterious portal that transports them to Nakali, a fantastical island filled with mythical creatures inspired by stories from their Filipino families. When they discover that returning home could come at the cost of losing the memories of their friendship, Jo and Raissa must find a way to leave the island without forgetting each other.

Forgotten Island features Filipino and Filipino-American talent including Tony Award-winning Lea Salonga, global comedy star Jo Koy, Grammy and Academy Award-winning H.E.R., actress Liza Soberano, and co-writer and co-director Januel Mercado.

“Great stories and great food both have a way of bringing people together,” said David Beal, Jollibee Group global chief marketing officer and head of digital marketing. “With DreamWorks Animation’s Forgotten Island, we’re inviting friends and families to celebrate the joy of friendship—from watching the film to sharing a delicious Jollibee meal together. It is a simple expression of what Jollibee has always stood for: serving great-tasting food and bringing the joy of eating to everyone.”

The Filipino connection extends beyond the film, with Filipino girl group, who are also Jollibee endorsers, BINI contributing the song “A Parallel World” to the Forgotten Island soundtrack. The upbeat electronic-pop track, which features English and Filipino lyrics, was released on July 23.

blocks.caption: Jollibee Forgotten Island BINI

blocks.text: BINI also performed the song at the Forgotten Island panel during San Diego Comic-Con in July, further connecting the group and the film with audiences around the world. The music video for “A Parallel World” also features Jollibee, showing members of BINI enjoying their favorite meals and sharing candid moments while in the United States for the song’s recording and related activities.
[insert video link]

“At Jollibee, we value partnerships that allow us to collaborate with world-class brands and create experiences that genuinely resonate with our customers,” said Dorothy Ching, vice president for marketing of Jollibee Philippines. “Our partnership with DreamWorks is especially meaningful because Forgotten Island brings together universal themes of friendship and family with Filipino-inspired storytelling. We are proud to be part of this global collaboration and excited to bring the spirit of the film to Jollibee communities around the world.”

The Jollibee and Forgotten Island collaboration brings together global entertainment, Filipino talent and storytelling, and Jollibee’s own spirit of togetherness, extending the experience from the big screen to everyday moments shared over a meal.
View this post on Instagram A post shared by Jollibee (@jollibee)
More elements of the collaboration are set to be revealed, including an exclusive Jollibee offer tied to the film. Details will be announced at a later date.
DreamWorks’ Forgotten Island arrives in theaters September 23, 2026.
For more information, visit https://www.jollibee.com.ph/ or follow Jollibee’s social media channels for updates.

articles.title: ‘Their boat was sinking’: RNLI vows to keep rescuing asylum seekers despite attacks
articles.summary:
Charity stresses small boat rescues are tiny part of its work and speaks out after volunteers abused by far-right agitators

The lifeboat charity RNLI has vowed to continue to rescue asylum…

blocks.text: The lifeboat charity RNLI has vowed to continue to rescue asylum seekers in the Channel despite attacks on volunteers and staff after the recent high-profile small boat landings.

RNLI bosses said workers had been subjected to online and physical abuse and there had been “baseless” rumours that the charity has housed asylum seekers or moved them to secret locations after helping them to shore.

The charity stressed that responding to small boats was only a tiny percentage of its work and updated its webpage explaining its work in the Channel, which includes powerful testimonies from volunteers involved in the operations.

RNLI staff and volunteers have been put in the spotlight over the charity’s involvement in a rescue on Sunday in which it a dinghy carrying asylum seekers was brought into Portsmouth, triggering protests by far-right agitators and local people.

Peter Sparkes, the RNLI chief executive, said that for more than 200 years the RNLI had rescued people without judgment, fear or favour. “Yet [staff and volunteers] and their families are being threatened by those who would hide behind a balaclava or a keyboard. Their action, in contrast, is wholly unacceptable in a civilised society.”
Sparkes said rumours that the RNLI housed asylum seekers on its premises, or that there were RNLI missions to move migrants to secret locations were “completely baseless and untrue”.
The charity said RNLI lifeboats launched 9,058 times in 2025 but only 109 of those launches were to small boats in the Channel, representing 1.2% of its rescue work.
The RNLI also said almost 95%, of those who crossed the Channel in small boats last year were picked up by the UK Border Force.

One of the testimonies on the RNLI’s small boats webpage came from Dan Sinclair, a volunteer helm at Walmer lifeboat station in Kent. He said: “One thing I would like people to understand is that these people genuinely need our help.”

Speaking about one rescue in the Channel, he said: “We launched to an overcrowded, unseaworthy small boat that was taking on water. One family was so scared. They were screaming. Their boat was sinking in front of their eyes. It was a horrible, horrible situation.

“We managed to rescue that family. We stopped them from drowning. There was a little girl on the boat. She looked me straight in the eye and said: ‘I love you, thank you.’ As a father, that went straight to my heart. That rescue cemented in my head that what we are doing as an organisation is exactly the right thing.”

blocks.caption: The RNLI has stressed that responding to small boats is only a tiny percentage of its work. Photograph: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images

blocks.text: Paula Lain, a volunteer lifeboat crew member at Dover, described another Channel rescue: “When I arrived on scene, it was a shock. There were people in the water, some disappearing under the water.

“There was this man holding on to the edge of the boat. He had no strength left. I leant over, lay on my front and I grabbed his arms, and he had no strength to hold me. I looked into his face and his eyes were wide, his face was grey. He was so scared.

“I just knew that if I let him go, he wouldn’t be there. I also knew that there was absolutely no way I was going to let him go. I held on to him and I called for help from my colleagues, and together we pulled him to safety.”
The charity said it responded to small boats in the Channel when HM Coastguard reported that people might be in danger at sea.

It continued: “International maritime law outlines that any vessel that becomes aware of people in distress at sea, must take all reasonable measures to assist. All small boats crossing the Channel are classed as being in distress.

“The RNLI is one of several declared search and rescue capability providers and, under long-established procedures, RNLI volunteer crews respond to anyone at risk of drowning, regardless of who they are or how they came to be in difficulty.

“The men, women and children who find themselves in distress and sinking in one of the world’s busiest shipping lanes are no exception. Our crews will go to their aid today when tasked, just like generations of lifeboat crews have done before them, in wartime and peace.

The charity rejected the accusation that it was a “taxi service” for asylum seekers. “We are not. HM Coastguard coordinates maritime search and rescue operations around the UK. Our lifeboat crews are tasked to assist people who are in difficulty, both in the Channel and around the coast of the UK.
“RNLI crews launch to the rescue, doing everything they can to save lives, without any thought to where the people they rescue are travelling from, nor their migrant status.”
