Lonnie G Bunch III announced he is stepping down as secretary of the Smithsonian Institution after seven years in the role amid Donald Trump’s unprecedented crackdown on the world’s largest museum’s autonomy.

articles.title: P6.2 billion slated for fertilizer, fuel aid to ease El Niño impact
articles.summary: On top of this, the Department of Agriculture is asking Congress for an additional P10 billion in its 2027 budget in anticipation of severe El Niño impact

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – The government is set to distribute P6.2 billion worth of fertilizer and fuel assistance to help cushion the impacts of the global oil crisis and El Niño on farmers and fisherfolk.
The fund is under the Unified Package for Livelihoods, Industry, Food, and Transport, or UPLIFT, a comprehensive response to energy security and livelihood needs amid the Middle East conflict.

There is no identified number yet of beneficiary farmers and fishers, according to Department of Agriculture spokesperson Arnel de Mesa. To ensure good yield, much of the fertilizer aid will be distributed to places less affected by El Niño.
“One of the things that DA is really going to do is to maximize yield in areas not affected by El Niño,” De Mesa said in a press briefing on Wednesday, September 9.

De Mesa said the full impact of El Niño on crops and prices will not be felt until the first semester of 2027, and that these measures are preparatory before El Niño develops into a more severe state by the end of 2026.
“If the fund is released in October, it works exactly as support during El Niño,” said De Mesa.
The Department of Agriculture is also requesting an additional P10 billion in 2027 to augment cash assistance for farmers and fishers, in anticipation of El Niño impacts.

The agriculture sector was left reeling from the effects of the southwest monsoon or habagat and past tropical cyclones, incurring production losses worth P4.38 billion. The palay sector lost P2 billion.
“Again, we do not see impact on rice prices because, in terms of volume, this is within our estimated losses every year because of typhoons, flooding, and other calamities,” De Mesa explained.
Estimated losses in rice production ranged from 500,000 to 600,000 metric tons, said De Mesa. The P2 billion worth of damage in the palay sector is “about only 70,000 metric tons of losses.”

In a bid to curb prices and support local production, the DA said it will not allow imports of high-grade rice in the meantime. According to reports, Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. talked with the rice industry to import only 25% (and above) broken rice. – Rappler.com
Quotes translated to English for brevity.

articles.title: Ben Shelton beats defending champ Carlos Alcaraz in U.S. Open match that ends after 3:30 a.m.
articles.summary: Ben Shelton had gone toe-to-toe with Carlos Alcaraz for five exhausting sets and finally, at 3:33 a.m. Wednesday, came the chance to end the U.S. Open champion's title reign.

image.caption: Ben Shelton, of the United States, celebrates after winning against defending tournament champ Carlos Alcaraz, of Spain, early Wednesday after their quarterfinal match at the U.S. Open in New York. (Heather Khalifa/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Tennis·New
Ben Shelton had gone toe-to-toe with Carlos Alcaraz for five exhausting sets and finally, at 3:33 a.m. Wednesday, came the chance to end the U.S. Open champion's title reign.
Shelton will play Francis Tiafoe in the semifinals — a matchup that guarantees an American man in the final
Ben Shelton had gone toe-to-toe with Carlos Alcaraz for five exhausting sets and finally, at 3:33 a.m. ET Wednesday, came the chance to end the U.S. Open champion's title reign.
Shelton fired an ace at 146 m.p.h. — a ball that Alcaraz couldn't have gotten back even with fresh legs.
That gave Shelton a 6-7 (5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6 (10-7) victory in a marathon tussle that was the latest-finishing match in U.S. Open history.
"I'm tired. It was a war," Shelton said. "Carlos is one of the greatest champions of our sport. It was the most enjoyable match I've had in my career, for sure."

Alcaraz had his 18-match winning streak in Grand Slam tournaments end in a match that lasted 4 hours, 28 minutes. He fought deep into the night and early into the next morning in a bid to get his hands on the trophy again, battling back even as he vomited before the start of the final set.
Alcaraz started the year winning the Australian Open, but was playing his first tournament since April after returning from a right wrist injury.
"I'm leaving happy and my head held high," Alcaraz said. "The truth is, I wanted to win … but also our goal was to leave the tournament having played matches and staying healthy."
The U.S. Open craves its night matches and players love the energy the fans provide — even when a number of matches have already gone past 2 a.m. this year.

Thousands stayed to the end, with Arthur Ashe Stadium perhaps still one-third full for the finish. Shelton benefited from a home-crowd boost even against the popular Alcaraz, with fans chanting his name along with "USA! USA!"

"It's incredible," Shelton said. "I always say that this is the greatest sports city in the world; I say that this is the greatest stadium in the world. I'm just hoping that my best friend and my sister over there don't have to be at work at 6 a.m. in three hours."

items: World women's No. 1 Sabalenka survives Noskova test to reach U.S. Open semifinals

blocks.text: Three of the four singles quarterfinals went to match tiebreakers on a marathon day, which started with Aryna Sabalenka edging Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova to keep her hopes alive of a third straight U.S. Open title.

Alcaraz had played in the previous latest finish at the U.S. Open when he outlasted Jannik Sinner in a match that finished at 2:50 a.m. in the 2022 quarterfinals, en route to his first Grand Slam title at 19.
Tiafoe storms back

Shelton, who won his second consecutive Canadian Open title last month, will next play No. 11 seed Frances Tiafoe, who kept coming back until he had reached his third U.S. Open semifinal, beating Alex Michelsen 5-7, 3-6, 7-5, 6-3, 7-6 (10-6).
Shelton seized control by winning nine straight games from early in the second set until he had a 3-0 lead in the third.
Alcaraz ran off four straight points in the tiebreaker to go ahead 5-3, but Shelton came back behind some of his powerful serves that can exceed 140 m.p.h., along with some mistakes from Alcaraz.
The Shelton-Tiafoe matchup guarantees a U.S. player will reach the men's final. The last Grand Slam title for an American man occurred in 2003, when Andy Roddick won the U.S. Open.
Tiafoe reached the U.S. Open semifinals in 2022 and it didn't initially appear he would be going back, as Michelsen continued his dominant run through his breakout tournament.
Michelsen won the first two sets and served with a 5-4 lead in the third, but couldn't finish it off. He hadn't lost a set in the tournament until Tiafoe stormed back.
Tiafoe said his performance to start the match was slow and flat.
"It wasn't good, let's put it that way. It wasn't good," he said. "Three out of five is a blessing, because you have time to get it together. I definitely waited for the last minute."
Michelsen, ranked No. 46, fell to 0-6 in matches that went to a fifth set.

It is also certain that a new U.S. Open's champion will be crowned, as none of Wednesday's quarterfinalists on the other side of the draw, led by top-ranked Alexander Zverev, has ever won the Grand Slam at Flushing Meadows, N.Y.
With files from CBC News

articles.title: South Korean students help plant narra seedlings on Mt. Malarayat
articles.summary: LUCENA CITY — South Korean students joined a regreening activity that involved planting 100 narra tree seedlings at the foot of Mount Malarayat in Lipa City, Batangas, the Department of Environment…

blocks.text: LUCENA CITY — South Korean students joined a regreening activity that involved planting 100 narra tree seedlings at the foot of Mount Malarayat in Lipa City, Batangas, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) said.

In a report on Tuesday, Sept. 8, the DENR office in Calabarzon said its Lipa community environment and natural resources office (Cenro) had partnered with ASEZ (Save the Earth from A to Z), a university student volunteer group of the World Mission Society Church of God, for the activity in Barangay Malitlit.
The agency said the initiative aimed to support the continuing rehabilitation and maintenance of the country’s forests.

“The program highlighted the important role of the youth in addressing environmental concerns, as well as the fact that environmental protection is a global responsibility that knows no nationality,” the DENR said.
Cenro Lipa also emphasized the importance of engaging young people in environmental protection efforts.
“It is important to raise their awareness and encourage their active participation in initiatives aimed at protecting the environment and natural resources,” the DENR said.

The narra, which is the Philippines’ national tree, is a large leguminous tree that can grow 30 to 40 meters tall. It produces fragrant yellow flowers that attract bees and typically blooms from February to May.
The species faces increasing threats from illegal logging, habitat loss, land conversion, and unsustainable harvesting. /mcm

articles.title: DOE files supplemental complaint against Leviste, SPBC officials
articles.summary: The Department of Energy (DOE), led by Secretary Sharon Garin, has filed a supplemental complaint in the estafa charges against Representative Leandro Leviste and two other officials of Solar Para sa…
articles.byline: JON VIKTOR D. CABUENAS, GMA News

blocks.text: Published September 9, 2026 6:21pm

The Department of Energy (DOE), led by Secretary Sharon Garin, has filed a supplemental complaint in the estafa charges against Representative Leandro Leviste and two other officials of Solar Para sa Bayan Corp. (SPBC).

DOE Renewable Energy Management Bureau legal officer Atty. Gabriel Corpuz confirmed that the supplemental complaint was filed at the Taguig City Prosecutor’s Office, as reported on dzBB’s “Super Balita sa Hapon.”

Supplemental complaint kaugnay sa reklamong estafa laban kay Cong. Leandro Leviste at dalawang iba pa, inihain ng @DOEgovph sa Taguig City Prosecutors' Office. #SuperBalitaSaHapon https://t.co/JQBiiAGYjG— DZBB Super Radyo (@dzbb) September 9, 2026

Corpuz declined to release a copy of the complaint, saying the Office of the City Prosecutor is still investigating the matter, but noted it relates to the estafa case against Leviste and SPBC officials Hazel Iris Lafuente and Irma Flaminiano

The supplemental complaint reportedly includes additional evidence against the respondents for SPBC's failure to deliver the awarded capacity in December 2025 and to maintain the performance security required for the first Green Energy Auction (GEA).
GMA News Online has also reached out to the DOE for further details on the supplemental complaint and Leviste for comment. No response was immediately available.
The DOE earlier filed a complaint with the Department of Justice (DOJ) against Leviste, Laguente, Flamiano, and other SPBC officials for alleged violations of the Public Service Act.
The complaint indicated that it had no records or receipt of any application by SPBC for permits, licenses, approvals, authorizations, or similar regulatory consents to fulfill its obligation.
Leviste then said the DOE’s allegations are baseless and a threat to public entities: “The only complaint I’ve seen is from the media, and based on that, I can say: super duper hina (very weak.)”
Under Republic Act 11357, SPBC was granted a nonexclusive 25-year legislative franchise, which would be deemed revoked if SPBC fails to operate continuously for two years.

Leviste, along with his mother, Senator Loren Legarda, is under investigation by the Ombudsman for plunder and graft complaints over the alleged failure of his renewable energy firm to provide solar power as required under its franchise.

They are both currently out of the Philippines, but Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla last month expressed confidence that they will return to the Philippines voluntarily, or in handcuffs. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: No travel tax, no budget: Can TIEZA keep its tourism projects alive?
articles.summary: The pesky travel tax is easy to hate, but abolishing it could leave multi-year tourism infrastructure projects in limbo, especially with TIEZA not getting anything in the proposed 2027 budget

blocks.text: The pesky travel tax is easy to hate, but abolishing it could leave multi-year tourism infrastructure projects in limbo, especially with TIEZA not getting anything in the proposed 2027 budget

Even as the government keeps pitching tourism as a growth priority and jobs engine, the agency tasked with building much of its infrastructure is heading into 2027 with billions’ worth of ongoing projects and a proposed budget of exactly zero.

On top of this, if Congress succeeds in abolishing the travel tax, the Tourism Infrastructure and Enterprise Zone Authority (TIEZA) could also lose the revenue stream that normally pays for almost everything it does.

A source familiar with TIEZA’s budget planning told Rappler that the agency initially sought around P5.2 billion in national government funding for 2027. That request covered infrastructure projects alone and did not yet include personnel services or maintenance and other operating expenses.

Budget Secretary Kim Robert de Leon informed TIEZA that the request could not be favorably considered because of the government’s limited fiscal space, the source said. Consequently, the proposed 2027 budget carries zero subsidy for the agency, compared with P248 million for general administration and support in 2026.
The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) echoed this stance during the budget hearing of the Department of Tourism (DOT).

“TIEZA’s proposal for National Government Subsidy in FY2027 is in view of several legislative measures proposing the abolition of the travel tax. However, as these bills remain under deliberation in the Senate and have yet to be enacted into law, the TIEZA’s requested subsidy was not considered in the FY [2027] NEP,” DBM Assistant Director Lulu Vispo said.

A zero budget may come with consequences on the tourism infrastructure pipeline. TIEZA chief operating officer Mark Lapid told lawmakers during the tourism department’s budget hearing that almost all of its projects are multi-year, with around P5.2 billion needed in 2027 alone to keep them moving.
The DBM, however, pointed to P2.355 billion in supposedly available TIEZA funds: P810.25 million in unobligated allotments as of March 31 and another P1.545 billion in unreleased 2025 appropriations.
“TIEZA may continue to utilize its travel tax collections to fund tourism-related infrastructures or projects,” Vispo added on Monday, September 7.

Meanwhile, TIEZA says that money is not sitting idly. Lapid told lawmakers that the roughly P2 billion cited during the hearing could not simply be used to pay for its infrastructure commitments as it was being used to fund the agency’s payroll.
“The P2 billion is for our personnel services in our office operations. So technically, we wouldn’t have any funds for infrastructure from the amount mentioned,” Lapid told lawmakers in Filipino.

blocks.caption: [In This Economy] Travel tax: Time to go

blocks.text: The problem is that the pesky P1,620 travel tax that travelers love to hate is also what keeps much of TIEZA running.
Congress is now moving to abolish it. The House has already approved House Bill 8464, while Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said in August that the Senate is targeting abolition within the year.

Under the current setup, 50% of tax collections go to TIEZA, 40% to the Commission on Higher Education, and 10% to the National Commission for Culture and the Arts. TIEZA’s share from those travel taxes makes up roughly 95% of its funding, an agency source told Rappler.

The House bill does anticipate the problem by requiring the national government to replace those funds through the annual budget. The tricky part is timing. TIEZA is being told to prepare for a future in which the travel tax disappears, but it has yet to receive approval for replacement funding.

blocks.caption: Photo from a TIEZA presentation shown during the House budget hearing for the DOT.

blocks.text: The tax cut could also have a very human cost inside the agency that needs consideration. A TIEZA presentation showed that around 300 travel tax personnel may be displaced out of its 1,045-strong workforce. Of those, 115 may have difficulty finding new work because of their age, while some 270 families could be affected.

Lapid told lawmakers that TIEZA cannot simply absorb the workers elsewhere because they are spread across international gateways nationwide and the agency does not have enough plantilla positions at its main office. Some could be terminated, while others may receive separation incentives.
During Monday’s budget hearing, the DOT made its case for Congress to restore an allocation for at least P1.3 billion for five TIEZA projects.
The list obtained by Rappler from a source includes:

items: P328.9 million for improvements of the Banaue Hotel and Youth Hostel complex in Ifugao. The TIEZA-owned property sits on a 5.3-hectare site overlooking the Banaue Rice Terraces and has 81 hotel rooms plus a 15-room youth hostel. TIEZA has been rehabilitating the aging property for years, which has remained temporarily closed.

P301.07 million for the CBDC River Water System in San Vicente, Palawan. This is meant to provide a long-term potable water supply to tourism establishments and communities around Long Beach, one of the main clusters of TIEZA’s San Vicente Flagship Tourism Enterprise Zone.

P400 million for iLIPAD, TIEZA’s airport development program with DOTr. Launched in 2020, the program helps fund upgrades to provincial airports, particularly facilities needed for night operations and greater flight capacity.

P212.2 million for the construction of a waste water treatment facility in Coron. The project is aimed at addressing the environmental strain that tourism and development place on one of Palawan’s busiest destinations.

P63.7 million for the construction of Sky Garden in Barangay Lucap, Alaminos City. The project, which Marcos himself broke ground for in May 2025, is envisioned as another attraction and gateway near Hundred Islands, with elevated gardens, viewing decks, walkways, parking, a commercial center, and a multipurpose hall.

blocks.text: The proposed allocations for the DOT and its attached agencies are not yet final, however, as Congress can still revise the 2027 budget before it is enacted. But so far, lawmakers have appeared receptive to calls for more tourism funding, repeatedly pointing to the country’s infrastructure gaps and the need for greater investment.

After all, one need only look at NAIA to see what years of underinvestment can do to a country’s main international gateway — and how quickly things can begin to turn once fresh capital finally starts pouring in. – Rappler.com

blocks.caption: Two years and billions later, has NAIA finally leveled up?

articles.title: Republicans in fight to hold on to majority look to ‘midterm convention’ to overcome Trump unpopularity
articles.summary:
Republicans plan to center the US president at the two-day event, while slamming Democrats as socialists

Republicans will gather in

blocks.text: Republicans will gather in Texas on Wednesday for a rare “midterm convention”, as they attempt to convince Americans to vote for a party led by a deeply unpopular president who has overseen price increases, inflation, and led the US into an increasingly unpopular war.

Donald Trump will dominate the two-day convention, appearing both nights as the GOP works to cling to control of the House of Representatives in November. Republicans plan to put the president at the center of the event, a bold strategy given his approval rating is hovering at about 38%, while accusing the Democratic party as being socialist and out of touch with Americans.

However, in a sign of Trump’s toxicity, some vulnerable Republicans have said they won’t attend the Dallas event: risking the potential ire of the president, but avoiding a public association with a deeply unpopular leader.

Less than two months out from the midterm elections, the Republican party faces a serious battle to retain its slender control of the House, while Democrats are increasingly hopeful they could pick up Senate seats. Winning either would put the Democratic party in position to stymie Trump’s aims during his final two years in office.

The convention represents perhaps Republicans’ final opportunity to make a large-scale, high profile pitch to Americans. Joe Gruters, the chairman of the Republican National Committee (RNC), which is organizing the convention, said the program will attempt to demonstrate how Republicans are “lowering costs, securing our border, making our communities safer, and putting American workers and families first”.

Whether voters buy that is a different matter, given costs, including gas prices, have risen during Trump’s presidency. Forecasters give Republicans a slim chance of holding onto the House, in particular, and some members of Congress have been keen to distance themselves from the event. Several Republican members of Congress said they will skip it entirely.

Hakeem Jeffries, the House minority leader, said a contingent of Democrats would also be in Dallas during the convention to “counter the falsehoods and extremism” on display in American Airlines Center.

Republicans facing close re-election bids have proved particularly likely to dodge the event, mindful that their Democratic opponents are looking for any opportunity to tie them to Trump. Tom Barrett, facing a close re-election fight in Michigan, and Zach Nunn, locked in a tight race in Iowa, are among those who have said they won’t be in Texas, and Thursday Axios reported that “only about 100 lawmakers and candidates are expected to attend.”

As well as risking association with Trump, there was the issue of cost. Multiple reports have suggested that House Republicans were being asked to donate at least $25,000 to the party to get a ticket.

Among the few who are confirmed to be attending are JD Vance and former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt, along with Ken Paxton, the Republican candidate for Senate in Texas who is polling neck-and-neck with Democrat James Talarico in a state that hasn’t elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1988.

There are signs too, that enthusiasm is low among the rank and file. The RNC announced in mid-August that Americans could apply for tickets to attend the event, suggesting that applicants would enter a lottery, and only a lucky few would be granted access.
Yet on Friday, days before the event was due to begin, applications for tickets were instantly being granted on an RNC sign-up page, suggesting the event was not yet at capacity.

Should the attendance be lacklustre, it will be a clear indictment of Trump himself, given RNC marketing materials in the build up had made it clear it was the president’s show. Indeed, some messages billed the event as “Trump’s midterm convention” – ditching the term ‘Republican’ altogether – while every press release has been at pains to stress Trump will be there both nights.
Trump himself was bullish about the convention in a podcast interview last week, telling the Texas lieutenant governor, Dan Patrick: “It’s going to be big stuff.”

articles.title: Homeland security agent charged with child rape in Alabama, officials say
articles.summary:
Kent Blacklidge, who officials say was ‘directly involved with child exploitation cases’, turned himself in last week

A federal law enforcement agent tasked with “trying to provide justice…

blocks.text: A federal law enforcement agent tasked with “trying to provide justice in cases involving kids” has been charged with child rape in Alabama, state authorities said on Tuesday.

Kent Blacklidge, described as a special agent with Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), turned himself over to the Baldwin county jail on 5 September in connection with a grand jury indictment charging him with first- and second-degree rape, sodomy and sexual abuse, police in the city of Spanish Fort said in a statement.

During a Tuesday news conference, Spanish Fort police chief John Barber said the charges against Blacklidge, 43, stemmed from an 11 January child sexual abuse report involving an underage girl. The Spanish Fort police statement said Blacklidge had been put on administrative leave by HSI as soon as officers began investigating the complaint against him.
Barber said Blacklidge was charged after officers conducted interviews and gathered other unspecified evidence into that complaint, about which the chief declined to release specific details.

“It takes an unbelievable amount of courage and strength for a victim of these types of crime to come forward,” Barber said at Tuesday’s news conference. “And I commend our victim for having that resolve.”

Alabama attorney general Steve Marshall said it was particularly disturbing to have to prosecute Blacklidge on child sexual abuse allegations because his responsibilities at HSI included “trying to provide justice in cases involving kids”.

He “was directly involved with child exploitation cases, working with these cases and raising awareness”, Marshall added. “That’s why it’s so profoundly disappointing and frankly disgusting that we stand here today and tell you that we charged him” with crimes that are incongruent with “what his professional responsibility was”.

Marshall further remarked: “It is also to be reaffirming to the public [that] it is our responsibility to follow the facts and apply the law regardless of what you’ve done, regardless of where you work and regardless of who you are.”

An attendee of Tuesday’s news conference told Marshall at one point that “we had covered” Blacklidge previously at a seminar where he provided training to local public school teachers about how to detect online predators targeting children for sex crimes.

The Alabama attorney general said his staff is handling the charges against Blacklidge because Blacklidge is a witness in some cases being prosecuted by the local district attorney’s office, requiring the latter agency to recuse itself.
Barber and Marshall each argued that Blacklidge’s charges should not reflect on the entire law enforcement field.
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which oversees HSI, did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the charges against Blacklidge.

But the DHS has faced scrutiny over its employee vetting practices after it received an unprecedented $170bn in funding for immigration and border enforcement securities amid the Trump administration’s drive for mass deportations.

The Associated Press reported in February that another agency under DHS’s purview, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), had seen at least two dozen of its employees and contractors be charged with various crimes since 2020.

Blacklidge by Tuesday had been released from jail on bond pending the outcome of his case, according to facility records. Remarks from Marshall on Tuesday suggested his bond amount had been set at more than $350,000.

As a condition of his release on bond, Blacklidge would have to submit electronic monitoring, home confinement, and an order to neither contact the victim in the case nor anyone else under the age of 18, Marshall said.
A message left for Blacklidge at a telephone number associated with him was not immediately returned.

articles.title: [DECODED] Why gamifying abuse impacts all of us
articles.summary: Gamified abuse scales the way it does not only because of the bad actors that exploit them, but for the lack of accountability from the online platforms in which they thrive

blocks.text: Gamified abuse scales the way it does not only because of the bad actors that exploit them, but for the lack of accountability from the online platforms in which they thrive

items: Rappler's investigation reveals NSFWPH, an online forum exploiting women by sharing non-consensual intimate content, boasting 430,000 members and a gamified system that rewards such behavior.
Members of NSFWPH take pride in manipulating women into sharing intimate photos, viewing their participation as a badge of honor, while the forum's ranking system incentivizes further exploitation.

The model of gamified abuse is not isolated to NSFWPH; similar practices are seen in the 'Grift Economy,' where online communities monetize vulnerability, highlighting a broader issue of accountability among platforms.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

In case you missed it, Rappler published a two-part investigative series over the weekend uncovering an online community that exploits women by sharing their intimate photos and videos without consent. The online forum called NSFWPH, which launched in April 2023, claims to have amassed 430,000 registered members and nearly 9 million posts and comments — all to share and consume voyeur content.

What’s more troubling, apart from the non-consensual sharing of intimate content featuring unwitting women, is that the members of this forum deliberately post and contribute to the forum as a point of pride.

Posts in the forum showed that many of the members of NSFWPH consider their participation a badge of honor, considering the lengths that they go to in order to obtain intimate photos and videos from women they know or interact with.
PART 1: How Filipinas’ intimate moments end up on a 430,000-member forum
Some even shared how they manipulated women into sharing nudes with them, which were in turn rewarded by the other forum members through congratulatory comments.

The forum treats these exploits, betrayals of trust, and, in some cases, content theft, as achievements that catapult a member’s “status” on the platform. The more a user shares and interacts on the platform, the more they get points that place them higher in NSFWPH’s ranking system.
This system has a name: it’s gamified abuse.

Because the higher a member ranks in the forum’s merit system, the more privileges they unlock, such as access to locked content or additional information about the victims, like their names or links to their Facebook and Instagram accounts.
Part 2: Gamified abuse: How a PH forum rewards submissions of non-consensual intimate content
In the case of NSFWPH, Filipinas were the victims. But the same business model is being used by bad actors across our current online ecosystem, targeting everyone vulnerable — including men.

Research and advocacy groups Reset Tech and Equimundo recently published a report called “The Grift Economy,” which examined how male loneliness is being monetized through membership schemes and so-called educational products. The report outlined how those in the “manosphere,” a collection of online communities focused on masculinity, are being pulled in with content that aligns with their ideologies, until they are drawn deeper into grievance-driven communities and, ultimately, monetized.

We see parallels in how the Grift Economy gamifies the exploitation of men’s need for connection to how the NSFWPH gamifies the exploitation of women’s intimate images and videos. Both employ these three mechanisms:

items: Points system turns participation into a game.

blocks.text: The NSFWPH forum gamifies its members’ participation by assigning them ranks. The Grift Economy explains how manosphere communities assign similar status systems in the “brotherhood” system. Such practice keeps members engaged, because they are rewarded through their participation.

items: Online platforms are active financial beneficiaries.

blocks.text: The Grift Economy points to online platforms as “usually the single largest financial beneficiary of any given operation.” This is because they share a portion of advertising income with the creators who run the ads that target vulnerable men.

In NSFWPH’s case, the result is a multi-layered monetization model. “The forum’s gamified system rewards users for uploading intimate content, while traffic and advertising turn exploitation into profit,” Rappler writers Gelo Gonzales and Lance Ariel Bustos said.

items: The problem is not limited to one platform.

blocks.text: Rappler’s investigation found that one of the most prominent members of NSFWPH is diverting the voyeur content he posts on the forum to a separate website where he set up pop-up ads that he can directly earn from, and to his own membership-based channel on Discord, a separate messaging and communication platform. By doing so, he is able to charge for more exclusive content.
The same is true for the Grift Economy. They thrive on different platforms, including YouTube, TikTok, X, Kick, Telegram, Instagram, and Spotify.

This practice makes the entire operation resilient: if one platform goes bust, other online communities will be able to absorb the operation, especially if they have lax policies against abuse and exploitation.

Gamified abuse is a business model, and it scales the way it does not only because of the bad actors that exploit them, but for the lack of accountability from the online platforms in which they thrive.
This makes all of us who spend time online vulnerable. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Family of killed teen call for death penalty in D4vd trial
articles.summary: The parents of Celeste Rivas Hernandez say execution "would be perfect" if D4vd is found guilty.

blocks.text: The lawsuit, lodged at Los Angeles Superior Court and reported by multiple, external US media outlets, external, makes similar claims to those raised by prosecutors in the criminal case against the singer.
Mercedes Martinez and Jesus Rivas allege that Burke caused the wrongful death, false imprisonment and childhood sexual assault of their daughter.
In the court documents, they say Burke and Hernandez first met in November 2023, when she was 13 years old.
Over the next 16 months, they claim, the pair would exchange almost 10,000 texts and have sex several times.

"At all relevant times Burke was an adult who occupied a position of authority over decedent, a minor, and was able to and did exercise undue influence and control over her," the parents say, in papers filed last Friday.

They go on to claim that Burke killed the teenager at his Hollywood Hills home, when she threatened to reveal their relationship, after allegedly sending a message that read: "I will end ur career and ur life".
In addition to Burke, the lawsuit names several of Burke's companies and managers, his mother and a live-in security guard.
Hernandez's parents allege that these people "enabled Burke to isolate" Rivas Hernandez and facilitated his travel, housing and security.
Burke's management company Mogul Vision and finance manager have previously denied knowing about Burke and Rivas Hernandez, the Los Angeles Times, external reported.

In July, a judge found enough probable cause for Burke to stand trial on the murder charge in the criminal case. At the time, the district attorney said he was weighing whether to seek the death penalty.
In a statement on Monday, which would have been Hernandez's 16th birthday, her family demanded that Burke be subjected to execution.

"If the death penalty were activated, it would be perfect for this kind of human being, devoid of feelings and emptiness inside, and without conscience, who only caused pain to our daughter, our family, and the world that supports our precious daughter," read the statement, released via the family's attorney.

Burke again pleaded not guilty to the charges last week and has since parted ways with his celebrity defence attorney. He is now being represented by a public defender and is due back in court on 19 October. His trial has been moved to next year.
Deputy public defender Walid Kandeel has said that Burke was "entitled to a defence that takes his circumstances seriously and carefully examines the evidence".
"We are committed to providing him with that defence," he said.
His office did not immediately provide comment on the civil lawsuit.

articles.title: Senators Tulfo want Sara Duterte to personally attend impeachment trial
articles.summary: Two majority senators, brothers Erwin and Raffy Tulfo, said they would prefer Vice President Sara Duterte to personally attend her impeachment trial and address the allegations against her.

blocks.text: Published September 9, 2026 5:48pm
Two majority senators, brothers Erwin and Raffy Tulfo, said they would prefer Vice President Sara Duterte to personally attend her impeachment trial and address the allegations against her.
This comes as the House prosecution panel announced that instead of presenting 15 witnesses, it would seek to have Duterte take the witness stand.
In an interview, Sen. Erwin Tulfo said the impeachment trial would be the proper venue for Duterte to respond to the allegations.
“Trial by publicity is really rampant now, especially on social media, including fake news. If fake news spreads quickly, you are immediately judged—you are called a thief, stupid, etc.," he said.
"Now this is the proper forum, the court, to explain your side, right? To give your side and, if you have to deny the allegations, then you have to deny them,” Tulfo added.
His brother, Sen. Raffy Tulfo, also said Duterte should personally address the allegations.
“Ideally, yes. It is better to hear it straight from the horse's mouth. She can address all our questions that her people cannot answer. She can answer them properly,” he told reporters.
However, Erwin Tulfo said inviting Duterte to attend the Senate impeachment trial was different from compelling her to appear.
He said Duterte could be invited but could not be forced to attend through a subpoena.
Erwin Tulfo cited the impeachment trial of former President Joseph Estrada, wherein Estrada was invited to attend but was not compelled to appear out of courtesy.
Meanwhile, Sen. JV Ejercito agreed that Duterte could not be compelled to attend.

“Well, it is the prerogative of the respondent, as they said, she is represented by her lawyers. So, it is up to her. We probably could not force her to go if she does not want to,” Ejercito said in a mix of English and Filipino.
Duterte is facing four articles of impeachment over allegations involving the misuse of confidential funds, bribery, unexplained wealth and threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

On Monday, the prosecution panel notified the impeachment court of its intention to present Duterte as a witness, saying the circumstances surrounding the allegations point to her as the “queen” on the chessboard, which can “move in all directions.”

“All of these pawns and castles and horses and bishops point to only one person, and that accountable person is the Vice President,” private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan said in her manifestation.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Conspiracy theories can provide answers, but not peace
articles.summary: Twenty-five years after 9/11, conspiracy theories about the terrorist attacks persist. But even as an attempt to make sense of a tragedy, psychologists say the benefit in conspiracy ideation or…

image.caption: Not even conspiracy theories help us come to terms with the unsettling events of September 11, 2001Image: Diane Bondareff/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Psychology is not an exact science. That may irk a few researchers in the field. But it is important to mention upfront: Researching the psychology of conspiracy theories — why people are drawn to believing them and the effect they have on those people — is a complicated field of research, and conclusions are difficult to derive.
That is due, in part, to one of the basic problems with psychology, whether it's in treatment or in research, and that is that it relies on people's self-awareness.

If we take the example of the 9/11 terrorist attacks, some people continue to maintain it was "inside job", orchestrated by a secretive and powerful club of evil doers in the US government, intent on controlling citizens' lives by fear. And that may be true. But it may also be true that you, as a believer in such a theory, have always felt powerful people — your parents or teachers — have controlled and curtailed your agency in life. You may even have a false memory of how the terrorist attacks evolved on that day in 2001. Then, if someone asked you, "What really happened?", could you really say it for sure? I couldn't.
Self-report data is an issue in conspiracy research
Whether as patients or participants in a study, we may be asked to "self-report" — to look inside ourselves and express how we feel and why.
Self-reporting is an established way of measuring conspiracies, said Neil Dagnall, a professor of psychology at Manchester Metropolitan University, in an interview with DW.
But self-report data are "not perfect," he added.

They can be difficult data to handle because each judgment a person makes about themselves is relative, inherently subjective, and open to outside influence and bias. People's answers can change from day-to-day, especially when they involve emotions or feelings about mental state, depending on a multitude of events and experiences in our lives. In addition, there is no common scale.

Say, for example, you and a friend were asked, "Are you happy?" You may both say "yes," but your reasons for doing so may be completely different and be subject to different variables. The same goes for a question like, "Do you believe in conspiracy theories?"

"The judgment I'm making is a relative one. What's my norm? Am I comparing it to my friends who don't believe in conspiracies or am I in a group of people who do believe in conspiracies? We're always making relative judgments about our psychological propensities," said Dagnall.
Which suggests we're unlikely to ever get a definitive answer. Self-report data suggest correlations, not causation.
In a study on conspiratorial beliefs and well-­being, which Dagnall co-authored and published in May 2026, "self-report data" was specifically highlighted as a limitation.

This makes it very difficult to assess whether "conspiracy belief" or "conspiracy ideation" is good or bad for people and their sense of well-being. Especially as people who seek and believe in conspiracy theories often start out with a skewed view of reality.
Brain health: How to protect mental fitness and memory
Observing behavior can offer clues
There are ways of "triangulating" self-­report data, as the authors of the study put it, to get a more reliable, objective reading of a person's emotional, or psychological, state.

For example, psychologists use behavioral observations, like measuring heart rate variability, or Galvanic Skin Responses such as the electrical conductance of a person's skin, which is affected by sweating under stress. You can also retest participants' self-reported data, and therefore its reliability, by asking the same questions at different points in time.

But there is another factor that complicates research into the psychology of conspiracy theories, and that is that they, and people who believe in them, are more common than we like to think or admit (even when we believe them ourselves).
"The idea that people who believe in conspiracies in general populations are remarkable or different is not true," said Dagnall.
The truth: 'conspiracies theories are common'

Most of us, at some point in our lives, are bound to see something strange or stressful in society and question whether we, as individuals or as a member of a group, accept the accepted truth of how that thing or event came about. It can be a healthy sign of a questioning mind.
There are positive examples of conspiracy theories that happened to kickstart investigations that then revealed the horrible truth of government corruption.
Take Partygate during the COVID pandemic in the UK or — the mother of all conspiracies — Watergate during the Nixon Administration in the US.
And there are other conspiracy theories, such as the one that nobody has ever landed on the moon, which you can either take seriously or laugh about.
It all comes down to "the degree to which we engage in conspiracies generally, and the extent to which they interfere and disrupt our everyday lives," said Dagnall.
For Dagnall, who doesn't believe in the 1969 moon landing, it doesn't seem to disrupt his daily life — at least, that is what he self-reported to DW.
Watergate Anniversary
But for some people, conspiracy theories are disruptive and can lead to a sustained sense of dissatisfaction.

"Ample studies suggest that exposure to conspiracy theories or belief in them might lead to more negative emotions, heightened anxiety, or even paranoid thoughts," said Zuzanna Molenda, a researcher at the Polish Academy of Sciences and lead-author of a 2023 study on emotion dysregulation and belief in conspiracy theories.

Some people may be primed to more readily believe in conspiracy theories because they generally struggle to deal with psychological threat and distress. When they then seek answers in conspiracy theories, their pre-existing negative psychology may be enhanced.

"If anything, the available evidence suggests that rather than help people manage difficult emotions, conspiracy beliefs may be accompanied by or contribute to further distress," wrote Molenda in an email to DW.
No long-term benefit from conspiracy belief
There may be some psychological benefit to conspiracy theories, said Molenda, but only in the short term.

"Conspiracy beliefs can provide people with a sense of explanation and understanding when events feel uncertain or difficult to make sense of. For some people, they might also be a source of entertainment and fun. For others, they can provide a sense of belonging and connection with others who share the same beliefs, and they can be an important part of social identity," Molenda said.
But these potential benefits do not necessarily translate into better well-being in the longer term, said Molenda.
In the end, we're all searching for meaning and purpose in life. If we find a satisfactory answer, it gives us, what psychologists call presense — a direction in life, and that is good.

But if your search only leads to more uncertainty, more anxiety, and more doubt in your purpose in life, then that's bad. "And people who believe in conspiracies are asking questions but not getting answers," said Dagnall.

articles.title: Run or hide? Benguet school tests active-attack response without fake gunfire
articles.summary: The drill was designed to test decisions, communication, police coordination, and recovery without using imitation weapons, simulated gunfire, or other hyper-realistic elements that could…

blocks.text: The drill was designed to test decisions, communication, police coordination, and recovery without using imitation weapons, simulated gunfire, or other hyper-realistic elements that could unnecessarily frighten learners

items: A nationwide school safety drill was conducted at Benguet National High School to prepare for active-attack incidents without using imitation weapons or simulated gunfire.
The drill involved various scenarios, including a suspected armed threat outside and a threat inside the school, with different responses based on the location of the threat.
Police officials emphasized the importance of ongoing preparedness beyond drills, including improving security measures and coordination among schools and emergency responders.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

LA TRINIDAD, Benguet — No fake gunshots rang through the campus and no one played an armed attacker. Yet classrooms locked down, some learners moved to safety, others hid, and police teams swept through Benguet National High School on Wednesday, September 9.

The exercise was part of a nationwide school safety drill for active-attack incidents, with Benguet National High School serving as the Cordillera ceremonial venue. It was designed to test decisions, communication, police coordination, and recovery without using imitation weapons, simulated gunfire, or other hyper-realistic elements that could unnecessarily frighten learners.

Forty senior high school learners took part in the exercise. Schools Division Superintendent Carmel Meris said parents were informed beforehand and signed waivers allowing their children to participate. Learners were also oriented before the drill, while participating agencies conducted a series of preparations ahead of the exercise.
“Today, we are gathering not because we expect an emergency to happen, but because we believe in being prepared before it happens,” assistant school head Eugene Espiritu told participants.

The drill was originally scheduled for September 3, to coincide with the nationwide active shooting drill of the Department of Education (DepEd), but was moved because of weather-related class suspensions.
The first scenario involved a suspected armed threat outside the school perimeter.
Security personnel were expected to recognize the threat, secure gates and access points, alert school authorities and law enforcement, and place the campus under a lockout.

Under the drill plan, learners and personnel were to remain inside secured buildings while outdoor activities and unnecessary movement were stopped. Teachers were tasked to keep learners calm and together, monitor official communications, and wait for verified instructions.
Police responders then simulated containing the threat before an all-clear was issued.
A separate scenario began with the threat already inside the school. This time, the exercise demonstrated that there was no single response for everyone.

One classroom, located away from the reported direction of the threat, practiced a controlled run response using a pre-identified safe route. Another classroom, positioned closer to the danger, practiced hiding and remaining inside a secured room.

The drill plan stressed that running and hiding were not sequential steps. Different groups could take different protective actions at the same time depending on the location of the threat, available information, and whether a safe escape route existed.
Once a full lockdown was declared, teachers were expected to account for learners while police took over the law-enforcement response.

Personnel from the La Trinidad Municipal Police Station acted as first responders, with additional support from the Benguet 2nd Provincial Mobile Force Company. Tactical operations remained under police authority, with the school instructed not to direct or interfere with the police response.
The drill did not end at “all clear.”
The exercise also tested what should happen after the immediate threat had been contained.
Police had to confirm that the designated area was secure before the school could begin a controlled transition out of lockdown.

Teachers then rechecked attendance and reported whether all learners were accounted for. Movement from classrooms was controlled, with learners brought to a reunification area rather than simply dismissed.

blocks.caption: SCHOOL DRILL. A teacher guides senior high school learners through the drill as they practice staying low, calm, and away from exposed areas during a simulated threat inside the school. Photo by Mia Magdalena Fokno

blocks.text: The drill plan also required verification before a learner could be released to a parent, guardian, or authorized representative.

Psychosocial first aid was built into the recovery phase for learners who might experience fear, anxiety, confusion, or emotional distress during the exercise. Participation in such support was voluntary, and learners were not required to recount or relive the simulated incident to receive assistance.

The school safety evaluation tool likewise required organizers to check whether the exercise was age-appropriate and trauma-informed and whether it avoided prohibited fear-inducing elements such as aggressor role-playing, imitation weapons, simulated casualties, and simulated gunfire.
Police officials said preparedness should go beyond completing a drill and include identifying ordinary security weaknesses that could matter in a real emergency.

La Trinidad police chief Lieutenant Colonel Zacarias Dausen said schools should continue strengthening control of entry and exit points, improve inspection procedures, and review CCTV coverage for possible blind spots.
He also stressed the importance of coordination among schools, police, disaster response teams, and medical personnel.

That accountability aspect was built into the evaluation tool, which covered not only learner behavior but also the school’s contingency plan, safe areas, evacuation routes, emergency communications, coordination with police, accountability procedures, medical services, and post-incident recovery.
Meris said district and school officials who observed the exercise were expected to bring the lessons back to their own areas and replicate the preparedness measures.
The point of the exercise, officials said, was not to make schools feel like places under siege.
It was to make sure that in the unlikely event of a serious armed threat, learners, teachers, and responders would not be encountering the procedures for the first time. – Rappler.com

articles.title: PNP to coordinate with French authorities in search for Zaldy Co
articles.summary: The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Wednesday said it is preparing to coordinate with French authorities in search for former party-list lawmaker Zaldy Co over plunder charges related to the…

blocks.text: Published September 9, 2026 5:38pm

The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Wednesday said it is preparing to coordinate with French authorities in search for former party-list lawmaker Zaldy Co over plunder charges related to the flood control scandal.

“The PNP is prepared to coordinate with French authorities through Interpol should former Congressman Zaldy Co be located abroad. We will provide full support to ensure that due process is observed and justice is pursued,” PNP chief Police General Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. said in a statement.

“If Mr. Co is arrested abroad, the process will follow international protocols through Interpol and diplomatic channels. The PNP will assist in the lawful transfer of custody once the court issues its directive,” he added.
Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla earlier said the Philppine authorities will follow up its request for an interpol red notice against Co in France.

The former lawmaker, former House speaker Leyte Representative Martin Romualdez, and two co-accused are facing P7.4-billion plunder charges before the Sandiganbayan over their alleged involvement in a kickback scheme involving flood control projects.

The PNP earlier said it has prepared a room for Romualdez in case he is allowed to remain under hospital arrest, after he was arrested on Monday at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan City.
Nartatez urged Co and the other co-accused to face the charges before the court.
"Evading arrest will not stop the process of justice. The PNP will continue to enforce warrants without fear or favor,” Nartatez he said.
“It takes time sometimes to enforce the arrest warrant but what is certain is that the long arm of the law always catches up with those who evade the legal processes,” he added.
PNP further said operations are ongoing to serve the arrest warrants against the two other co-accused. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: UK rules out cyberattack after major flight disruptions
articles.summary: Airports across the UK continue to face delays and cancellations after a flight processing system failure. The UK's transport secretary has summoned the CEO of National Air Traffic Services (NATS)…

image.caption: Hundreds of thousands of passengers were affected by the air traffic disruptions on Tuesday Image: Jonathan Brady/PA Wire/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Martin Rolfe, CEO of the UK's National Air Traffic Services (NATS), on Wednesday ruled out a cyberattack after a major interruption Tuesday in operations at British airports.
"We will be doing a very, very thorough and full investigation," Rolfe told the BBC.

More than 1,000 flights were cancelled and delayed due to air traffic control problems that started Tuesday morning and lasted for several hours. NATS said a problem involved an issue with the flight processing system.
Although NATS said the problem was resolved, more than 150 flights were cancelled on Wednesday, and more delays were expected throughout the day.
London's Heathrow Airport on Wednesday said "some disruption may continue as airlines reposition aircraft and crew," and advised travelers to check flight status before heading to the airport.

"There are going to be dozens of cancellations in the morning of flights coming into Heathrow because, basically, the flights didn't go out tonight," travel journalist Simon Calder said to Sky News. "The consequences will be horrible," he added.
Questions over the UK's network
The UK's Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander said Wednesday that she had summoned Rolfe for a closer explanation of what caused the malfunction, amid concerns over the UK's air traffic network.

This is not the first time a major system failure has affected British airports. In August 2023, several flights were cancelled due to a "system meltdown," costing airlines $135 million. In 2025, problems with flight radars affected several airports in the UK, including Heathrow Airport.
"I am seeking assurances that lessons will be learned and systems that support aviation are up to the ‌job," Alexander said on X.

blocks.caption: irports across the UK faced delays and cancellations after a flight processing system failure.Image: Jonathan Brady/PA Wire/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Ryanair, Europe's biggest airline, said at least 150,000 passengers using its services experienced delays of up to eight hours. Two hundred of its flights were cancelled.
For the second time, the airline demanded that NATS CEO Rolfe resign.
Rolfe told Sky News he accepted "full responsibility" but did not say if he was considering stepping down.

NATS provides air control traffic services to 15 UK airports. It is a public-private partnership which is partially owned by airlines including British Airways and easyJet, pension funds and the government.

articles.title: FACT CHECK: No Turkish police deployed to secure BARMM polls
articles.summary: Election watchdog groups pointed out that Turkey was invited to send election observers, not police officers

blocks.text: Claim: Turkish police will guard the first parliamentary elections in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) and arrest violators of election laws.

Why we fact-checked this: The Facebook page “Bagong Kapantay Moro” claimed in a September 6 post that Turkish police officers will be deployed to secure the upcoming BARMM parliamentary elections on September 14.
The post reads: “Turkiyé polis (sic) magbabantay sa kauna-unahang parliament election sa BARMM? Upang panatilihin na walang dayaan sa eleksyon. Huhuliin nila ang lalabag at mandaraya.”
(Turkish police will guard the first parliamentary elections in BARMM to prevent cheating. They will arrest violators and cheaters.)
The post also alleged that Turkey was intervening because most media organizations were supposedly “fake.” As of writing, the post has garnered around 2,000 reactions, 434 comments, and 853 shares.
Some commenters appeared to believe the claim. One thanked foreign countries for supposedly helping the United Bangsamoro Justice Party and the Bangsamoro.

The facts: Election watchdog groups Independent Election Monitoring Center – BARMM and the Institute for Autonomy and Governance debunked the claim in a September 8 Facebook post, and urged the public to verify claims about supposed foreign involvement in the elections.

“This is false. No foreign police force, including Türkiye’s, can be deployed to enforce, patrol, or police another country’s elections. Election security in BARMM remains the responsibility of [Commission on Election]-BARMM, the Armed Forces of the Philippines, and the Philippine National Police,” the post read.

The watchdog groups pointed out that the viral claim likely misrepresents a real appeal from Moro Islamic Liberation Front chairman Ahod “Al Haj Murad” Ebrahim. Inquirer.net reported that Ebrahim, in an August 30 letter ahead of the September 14 polls, called on foreign governments and international organizations to send election observers.

The same report mentioned that Turkey was among the diplomatic missions invited to participate, but the invitation was for observers, not police officers. The invitation made no mention of granting foreign personnel the authority to make arrests or conduct security operations.

The Commission on Elections (Comelec) opened the BARMM election to local and international observers under Resolution No. 11247. Accredited observers may monitor different stages of the election, subject to Comelec’s rules. Observers must also remain impartial and free from political, economic, or other conflicts of interest.
As of writing, there are no public statements issued by the Turkish Embassy in Manila or Turkey’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs regarding the invitation.

Unrelated photo: A reverse image search using Google Images traces the photograph to o the Daily Sabah’s April 10 report on the Turkish Police Organization’s 181st anniversary, which says the photo is credited to Anadolu Ajansi (AA). Other AA photos of the same event can be found on Anadolu Images and Reuters.
The original caption places the police parade in Kayseri, Turkey, on April 10, 2026. The image does not show Turkish police officers preparing for deployment to secure the BARMM polls.

Securing the elections: The first-ever BARMM parliamentary elections will be held on September 14, marking a historic milestone in the region’s transition from the 2014 peace agreement between the Philippine government and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) to a functioning parliamentary system. (LIVE UPDATES: First BARMM parliamentary elections)

The election also comes amid real security and turnout concerns. Monitoring groups have flagged a rise in gun-related incidents and voter uncertainty over the new parliamentary system, warning that these could affect turnout and public confidence in the polls.

To address security concerns, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. approved the deputation of Philippine law enforcement agencies through Memorandum Order No. 48. The government’s security plan for the elections includes nearly 9,000 Philippine National Police officers, five joint task forces deployed by the Armed Forces of the Philippines, and Philippine Coast Guard support.
Debunked: Rappler has previously debunked other false claims involving BARMM officials, as well as other disinformation about Philippine elections:

items: FACT CHECK: BARMM official’s ‘hate quote’ after MSU bombing is fake
FACT CHECK: ‘News reports’ on Bayan Muna disqualification are fabricated
FACT CHECK: 2025 midterm elections on May 12, no date change
FACT CHECK: Local surveys showing Duterte family, others winning, are fake — Pulse Asia

blocks.text: – James Bones/Rappler.com
James Bones is a Research and Data volunteer at Rappler. He is a fourth-year Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering student at the Polytechnic University of the Philippines – Manila.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: Man shot dead in Sydney community centre carpark
articles.summary:
NSW police say a vehicle was seen driving away from the scene in Punchbowl in the city’s south-west

A man has been shot dead in a carpark of a Sydney community centre in the city’s…

blocks.text: A man has been shot dead in a carpark of a Sydney community centre in the city’s south-west.
Emergency services were called to the community centre on Rossmore Avenue, in Punchbowl on Wednesday evening, following reports of a shooting.
A vehicle was seen driving away from the location after the fatal shooting, NSW police said in a statement.
Paramedics treated the man but he died at the scene. He is yet to be identified, police said.
The fatal shooting comes two days after the NSW premier, Chris Minns, announced measures to curb gangland violence in Sydney.
Under the new laws being introduced in the state, new aggravated offences for conspiracy to commit gang-related murder. The maximum penalty will be increased to life imprisonment.

The government has repeatedly denied criminal gangs are “out of control” in the city after the mistaken identity shootings of electrician Joshua Macdonald and Marco Tapia, a 23-year-old biomedical engineering student last week.
Police said neither man had any link to organised crime.

New laws being introduced in New South Wales aim to tackle organised crime by giving police more power and introducing new aggravated offences for conspiracy and attempted murder, with the maximum penalty increased to life imprisonment.

Police would also be able to use new interim serious crime prevention orders to restrict people suspected of serious and organised crime. Those would be applied while the state’s supreme court considers the full order.
Children’s indictable offences would include activities linked to organised crime, and public shootings and firebombings would be added to the scheme.
In a statement on Monday, Minns said people who conspire to arrange a gangland murder should face the prospect of “spending the rest of your life behind bars.”
“We want to hit these criminal networks at every point – the people who organise the violence, the people who facilitate it online and the people who ultimately carry it out,” he said.
Police are urging anyone with information about the Punchbowl incident to contact Campsie police station or Crime Stoppers.

articles.title: 3 Degamo slay suspects convicted in firearms, explosives cases
articles.summary: The three suspects were previously identified as former soldiers who are all “highly skilled” in military operations.

blocks.text: September 9, 2026 | 5:11pm
Suspects in the killing of former Negros Oriental Governor Roel Degamo arrive at the Department of Justice to attend the preliminary investigation in Manila on June 13, 2023.
The STAR / Ernie Penaredondo

MANILA, Philippines — Three suspects linked to the 2023 killing of Negros Oriental Gov. Roel Degamo were convicted in separate cases involving illegal possession of firearms, ammunition and explosives, the Department of Justice said Wednesday, September 9.

In a statement, the DOJ said the Manila Regional Trial Court Branch 40 found Joric Garrido Labrador guilty beyond reasonable doubt of violating Section 28 of Republic Act 10591, or the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act.
The court also convicted Joven Calibjo Javier and Benjie Rodriguez of unlawful possession of explosives under Section 3 of Presidential Decree 1866, as amended by Republic Act 9516.
Labrador was sentenced to eight years, eight months and one day to 10 years, eight months and one day in prison, while Javier and Rodriguez were each sentenced to reclusion perpetua.
The three suspects were previously identified as former soldiers whom then-Army chief Romeo Brawner Jr. described as "highly skilled military operators."
The DOJ said a .45-caliber pistol, two magazines, 14 rounds of live ammunition and two hand grenades were recovered from the suspects.
In a social media post, Rep. Janice Degamo (Negros Oriental, 3rd District), wife of the slain governor, welcomed the court's decision.
"Every conviction is a step forward. Every person held accountable brings us closer to the truth and to the justice that Roel and every victim of the Pamplona Massacre deserve," the lawmaker said.
On March 4, 2023, Degamo and nine others were shot dead when armed men attacked his residence in Pamplona, Negros Oriental, during the distribution of government aid. Dozens of others were wounded.
Ten suspects in the killing eventually recanted earlier statements linking former lawmaker Arnolfo Teves Jr. to the attack.

Labrador, Javier and Rodriguez were among those who withdrew their previous statements. The suspects alleged they had been tortured and coerced into making the statements, allegations authorities denied.
Teves, whom prosecutors accuse of being among the masterminds of the attack, has denied involvement in the killings.

He remains detained at the Metro Manila District Jail in Camp Bagong Diwa, Taguig City, as he faces separate murder, frustrated murder and attempted murder charges in connection with the Degamo attack.

articles.title: Prosecution: Calling in VP Sara as witness in her impeachment trial is due process
articles.summary: The House prosecution panel"s plan to call Vice President Sara Duterte as one of the witnesses in her impeachment trial is part of due process, House prosecutor Joel Chua of Manila said Wednesday.

blocks.text: Published September 9, 2026 5:08pm
The House prosecution panel’s plan to call Vice President Sara Duterte as one of the witnesses in her impeachment trial is part of due process, House prosecutor Joel Chua of Manila said Wednesday.
Chua made the statement a day after private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan informed the Senate impeachment court that the prosecution reserves its right to present the Vice President as a witness.

“We are considering calling her in since the Vice President has been saying that she is innocent; that this is just political harassment. If she can sit on the witness stand and explain, then she can answer the questions of the Senator-judges and even the public,” he said.
“Kung hindi siya darating, masasabi natin na na-miss niya 'yung chance na para makapagpaliwanag sa ating mga kababayan,” he added.
(If she won’t do it, then we can say that she will miss her chance to explain her side to the public.)

Besides, Chua said, all of the Vice President’s subordinates, namely Gina Acosta, Lemuel Ortonio, and Michael Poa, all said that it was the Vice President who is knowledgeable about how at least P612.5 million in confidential funds of her office were spent.

“All the witnesses from her officials from her office said they do not have an idea how the confidential fund was spent. Even the Special Disbursing Officer [Acosta], who should know about the fund’s disbursement, did not know how it was disbursed. With that, it is only the Vice President who can answer such disbursement queries,” Chua said.

The lawmaker then said that while the Vice President cannot be forced to testify as a witness in her impeachment trial, she can always appear voluntarily, just like what the late former Chief Justice Renato Corona did in his 2012 impeachment trial.
Chua, however, assured the public that the prosecution’s case is airtight, with or without the Vice President taking the witness stand.

“Whether she takes the witness stand or not, we have a strong case anchored on evidence, as you have seen in our allegation of grave threat [against President Ferdinand Marcos, Jr. and his family], as well as alleged misuse of confidential funds,” he said. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Marcos to join BRICS Summit in India
articles.summary: President Marcos Jr. is taking ASEAN's agenda to BRICS as emerging powers meet in India.

blocks.text: September 9, 2026 | 5:07pm

Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos (R) shakes hands with India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi during the ceremonial reception at India’s presidential palace Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi on Aug. 5, 2025.
AFP / Sajjad Hussain

MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. will attend the 18th BRICS Summit in India on September 12 and 13, where he plans to take the Philippines' priorities as this year's ASEAN chair to a bloc of the world's biggest emerging economies.
Marcos and First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos are going at the invitation of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the Department of Foreign Affairs said Wednesday, September 9.

"Through this visit, the president seeks to ensure that our modern partnerships remain open, resilient, and capable of delivering prosperity to our people," DFA spokesperson Analyn Ratonel said at a Palace press briefing.
Marcos will use the summit to lay out the priorities set by the Philippines for ASEAN, such as peace and security and development.
The trip also opens the door for the Philippines and ASEAN to talk trade, investment, regional security and climate resilience with the larger emerging economies, she added.
Modi meeting, business pledges
On the sidelines, Marcos is expected to meet Modi to go over the Philippines-India Strategic Partnership and review how the two countries are carrying out their five-year plan for 2025 to 2029.
The two leaders will also exchange views on economic issues affecting their countries, Ratonel said.

Marcos will separately meet Indian business leaders to follow up on the pledges and commitments worth $5.8 billion that Indian firms announced during his state visit to India in August 2025. Those covered technology, health, energy and infrastructure.
Foreign Affairs Secretary Theresa Lazaro, Information and Communications Technology Secretary Henry Aguda and acting Finance Secretary Frederick Go are joining the delegation.
BRICS is an informal group of emerging economies, its name being an acronym of Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa.

articles.title: Kitty Duterte calls for accountability, thanks supporters amid VP Sara's legal battles
articles.summary: Following the arrest warrant issued against her sister, Vice President Sara Duterte, Veronica “Kitty” Duterte on Wednesday thanked their family"s supporters and called for accountability.

blocks.text: Published September 9, 2026 5:02pm Updated September 9, 2026 5:30pm
Following the arrest warrant issued against her sister, Vice President Sara Duterte, Veronica “Kitty” Duterte on Wednesday thanked their family’s supporters and called for accountability.
“Managot ang dapat managot,” Kitty Duterte said. (Those who are accountable should be held accountable.)
A video from GMA News’ Vonne Aquino showed Kitty saying the phrase during a general assembly for the Inday Sara Movement Philippines at the Club Filipino in San Juan City.
The phrase has been used across the political spectrum, with both administration allies and critics using it.

“I would like to thank everyone gathered here today for the Inday Sara Na Movement Philippines. I would also like to thank everyone for the unwavering and continuous love and support,” Kitty said in a video message.

“The country needs it now more than ever. Do not let the sacrifices and the hardships of our fellow men be in vain. Managot ang dapat managot. Walang iwanan. Babalik tayo sa 2028, (Those who accountable must be held accountable. No one will be left behind. We will return in 2028).
Sara Duterte has already announced her intention to run in the 2028 presidential elections, with many surveys naming her as the frontrunner.
However, the Vice President is facing both an impeachment case at the Senate and a grave threats case before the Quezon City court.

The Quezon City Regional Trial Court has already issued an arrest warrant against Duterte over the threats she made against President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr., First Lady Araneta-Marcos and former House speaker Martin Romualdez. She posted bail for the charges on Saturday.

It is not just Sara facing legal issues. Her father, former president Rodrigo Duterte is currently detained in the International Criminal Court in The Hague, Netherlands awaiting trial for crimes against humanity in relation to his bloody drug war that saw at least 6,000 people dead, with human rights groups saying that the number could be as high as 30,000.
Pro-Duterte supporters to show up for Sara
In a report from DZBB’s Sam Nielsen, ISMP founder Daniel Nobieza said that they will accompany the Vice President when she attends her arraignment at the Quezon City Regional Trial Court on Friday.

“Siguro more than 300, approximate po, kasi yung iba po kasi hindi nakadalo ngayon, sa Friday po pupunta para po makita po ni VP na solido pa rin po ang suporta ng kanyang mga volunteers at followers,” Nobieza said.

(Maybe more than 300, it is approximate, because some of us were not able to go today, so they will go on Friday so that the VP could see that the support of her volunteers and followers is still solid.)

Nobieza said that they have accepted that more unexpected things could happen, such as new cases being lodged against Duterte. However, they have already accepted this fact especially with the 2028 elections approaching.
Nobieza said that they are in the process of obtaining a rally permit. —RF, GMA News
